This is the email I wrote to XXXX : I am writing to formally request your assistance regarding unjustified charges applied to my recent car rental through XXXX, booked via XXXX. When I reserved the vehicle, the stated and agreed upon total was {$220.00}, a price confirmed as final. 

Upon arrival at the XXXX airport, the counter agent updated the total to {$310.00} after including toll charges, which already seemed excessively high.Despite my objections and suggestion to handle tolls directly, I was informed of an additional {$10.00} fee per toll if not processed through XXXX, prompting me to accept the toll charge of {$74.00}. However, this does not account for an unexplained surplus of {$20.00}, contradicting the agent 's assurance that no other fees would be added. 

Furthermore, upon exiting the rental facility, another agent presented a final charge of {$410.00} a stark and inexplicable increase from just moments before. This sequence of charges not only lacks transparency but suggests a deliberate overcharge. Such practices are not only unethical but potentially fraudulent. She was very rude and would not explain to us why the charge went up. 

Given these circumstances, I am compelled to dispute these charges through my credit card company unless a full refund of the unwarranted fees is processed promptly. I urge your immediate attention to this matter to avoid further escalation and to maintain customer trust and satisfaction. 

Please confirm the processing of my refund at your earliest convenience. Thank you for your prompt attention to this serious matter. 

I submitted to BOA as a fraud claim and they denied it saying I signed the receipt which is not true. I did not sign anything upon leaving the parking lot when the price was unjustly raised.

_source.complaint_what_happened:
On XX/XX/XXXX I was looking to purchase a flight on the Delta website. On the site was an advertisement with to Earn a {$400.00} Statement Credit when you sign up for the Delta Sky Miles Gold American Express Card. In the advertisement, they showed the price of the flight I was planning to purchase minus the amount of the AMEX statement credit implying that I could apply for the card and then continue on to purchase the flight. 

I clicked on the ad and applied for the credit card. Instead of being instantly approved ( I have excellent credit ), I was notified that it would take time to learn if I was approved, ( up to 14 days is what I remember. ) At that point I had already provided all my information and since I had found the flight I wanted at a good price and was concerned that the price may go up or that the flights I wanted might not be available later, I decided that I needed to purchased the flight on a different credit card. 

The next day ( XX/XX/XXXX ) I saw that I had an email that I had been approved for the Delta Sky Miles Gold American Express Card and that I needed to accept the card. Since I had only applied to get the card because of the advertised promotion which required purchasing a Delta flight on the card in order to receive a {$400.00} statement credit, and because I was within the 24 hour, free cancelation period for the flight I'd purchased, I called AMEX to confirm that once I accepted the AMEX card Id been approved for that I would have the card information I would need to purchase my flight. I provided the reference number from the email from AMEX which said I had been approved and told the rep that I wanted to use the card right away to purchase my flight. He told me that if I accepted the card I *might* get the card number right away and be able to use it to purchase my flight, but that more likely, I would have to wait 7-10 business days to receive the physical card in order to use t to purchase my flight. When I explained the time constraints involved, ( 24 hour cancellation policy, fluctuating price and flight availability ), and that I couldnt wait 7-10 days to purchase the flight he suggested that I call Delta to see if they could hold the flight for me or something similar to allow me to wait for the physical credit card.

I decided to accept the card and hope that I would be provided with the information I needed to cancel and re-book the flight. I was not. I then called AMEX again as a last ditch effort to try and get the information necessary to purchase my flight while I still had the ability to cancel and re-book. I was told that all they could do was expedite the shipping of the card, but to do that, I would have to call back after 24 hours.

In conclusion, because of AMEXs deceptive advertising, I provided them with my financial information and signed up for a credit card that I didnt need because their advertising implied that once I applied and was approved, that I could immediately use the new card to purchase the very flight I was currently looking at. Instead I now have to decide if I want to cancel the flight that I booked on a different card, wait 9 days or more and then try and re-book the same flight and hope that its still available and that the price hasnt increased.

XXXX XXXX SSN : XXXX Subject : Notice of Identity Theft and Request for Debt Validation and Cease Communication I am writing in response to your recent letter regarding the fraudulent account opened in my name. I appreciate your attention to this matter, but I must address several points in your response that indicate a misunderstanding of the situation and the documents I have previously provided. 
1. Identification Information : You stated that the identification information provided at the time of the account opening belongs to me. As outlined in the police report and the letter from my commanding officer that I attached, my identity, including my ID, passport, wallet, and other personal information, was stolen. Had these documents been thoroughly reviewed, it would be clear that it is impossible for me to have opened the account. 
2. Address on Application : You mentioned that the address listed on the application is mine. While this is correct, I was not residing at that address during the time the account was opened. I was stationed at XXXX XXXX XXXX in XXXX, as evidenced by the XXXX XXXX  included in my documentation. Therefore, it is evident that someone else used my stolen information and address to execute this fraudulent act. 
XXXX. Mailed Credit Card : You claimed that the credit card was mailed to my address. Given that I was XXXX and not at the address, the individual who stole my information likely intercepted the mailing. This would have been easy for them to do, given my absence and the significant time zone difference, which limited my ability to monitor such activities. 
XXXX. Email Address : You stated that the application matched an email address, presumably XXXX. I have not had access to this email since XXXX. My current email address is XXXX, as I have already communicated. 
5. Payment Matching My Account : You noted that a payment was received from an account ending in my name. If my identity has been stolen, it is entirely plausible that multiple fraudulent accounts and payments could be made using my information without my consent or knowledge. 
Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) and Georgia state laws, I have the right to dispute and request validation of any debt that is claimed to be mine but is the result of identity theft. I also have the right to request cessation of any communication regarding the disputed debt and its removal from my credit reports. 
1. Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) ( 15 U.S.C. 1681c-2 ) : This federal law provides protection for victims of identity theft, including the right to request a block on any fraudulent information resulting from identity theft from their credit reports. Credit reporting agencies must comply with this request upon receiving appropriate documentation. 
2. Georgia Code Title 10, Chapter 1, Article 19 ( 10-1-911 et seq. ) : Georgia state law provides specific remedies for identity theft victims, including the right to file a police report and dispute fraudulent accounts. Under this law, once identity theft is reported, debt collectors must cease collection efforts on the fraudulent debt. 
XXXX. Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) ( 15 U.S.C. 1692 ) : This act prohibits debt collectors from using unfair, deceptive, or abusive practices to collect debts. Under the FDCPA, I am requesting that you cease all communication with me regarding this fraudulent account and remove it from any credit reporting agencies ( CRAs ). 
Request for Action Given the evidence provided and my rights under the FCRA, FDCPA, and Georgia state law, I am requesting the following actions from [ Company Name ] : 1. Cease Communication : Immediately cease all forms of communication with me regarding the disputed account referenced above. 
2. Validation and Removal : Investigate the identity theft claim and remove any record of this account from my credit report with all CRAs. 
3. Confirmation : Provide written confirmation that this account has been removed and that you will cease all collection activities related to this account. 
I expect your prompt cooperation in resolving this matter. Please address all correspondence to my address provided above. Failure to comply with these requests will leave me no choice but to pursue further legal action to protect my rights. 
Thank you for your immediate attention to this urgent matter. 
Sincerely,

On XX/XX/XXXX, I called again and spoke to someone in fraud named XXXX, who clearly saw what happened. Based on his statements, the information noted to the account was incorrect. He said that " someone called to report my death. '' I explained to him that that someone was me calling to report my brothers death on his account. 

He took his time and reviewed my account, and explained to me that they would reverse all of the charges, since they were erroneous, and made while my account was suspended and closed. He stated that he saw the error that was made on their part with the reporting. He also said that he was escalating it and that I would receive a letter in the mail in the next 30 days that would show that they have made the necessary corrections with the credit bureaus. _source.complaint_what_happened:
Dispute with Bank of America on credit card charges. 
Disputed Claim Number : XXXX ( Tried to resolve this directly with Bank of America ) Account Ending in XXXX ; XXXX XXXX XXXX Im reaching out to CFPB after being failed multiple times by Bank of America on a disputed claim. I have spent well over six months ( beginning in the Fall of XXXX ) trying to resolve my dispute but have gotten nowhere. 

In XX/XX/XXXX, I noticed a discrepancy on my credit card statement online and I called Bank of America Customer Service to notify them of a disputed claim. The vendor was XXXX. In speaking to Customer Service, it was brought to my attention that these were transactions over multiple months ( I believe, per BOA, the first one was in XX/XX/XXXX ). I categorically denied ever using this vendor and on the call, they mentioned they would send me receipts/proof that I have. To date, I am yet to receive this proof that I have used this vendor, which I understand is based in MA ( I live in XXXX ). 

I have subsequently called Customer Service multiple times and even asked to be directed to speak to a supervisor. Each time I get a new reason why the claim was denied either I didnt relay the exact number of times I noticed this transaction on my cc statements ( please note with the first call in XX/XX/XXXX, I asked customer service to check for me ), or since I paid my credit card bills on time, I should have known, or I accessed my online banking the exact same number times as the number of times the transaction has taken place, so I should have known. 

Each time I speak to a supervisor, they agree that paying credit cards on time and other reasons stated is not grounds for denying a claim. I even have relayed that over the span of the months the vendor was used, I have been out of the country and so it was impossible for me to use that vendor. Also as soon as I reported the fraud and the cc at the time was cancelled and I received a new one, there were no further transactions with this vendor. Finally I have always paid my bills and never disputed a claim before. All these aspects point to a strong case of cc fraud. 

XXXX was particularly hard year for me personally ( my sister died of XXXX and I was her XXXX XXXX, my husband has an XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX and my daughter was diagnosed with XXXX XXXX ). Im relaying this to you not for sympathy but for context that my only intention in XXXX was to be in survival mode- that included paying bills on time to not affect my credit score. I did not pay attention to the details of the statements. Im not sure why I need to be penalized for paying my bills on time!! 

With repeated denials on my fraud claim and with no rationale reason, I searched online to find a way to escalate the issue. I reached out to the Client Care team ( XXXX ). This Monday ( XX/XX/XXXX ), I connected with a member of their team. In speaking with her, she said BOA can not do anything as I signed an agreement with XXXX saying it was my responsibility to check my statements each month and report fraud. I have not received documentation of where I have signed for this. In addition, they don't have data that goes that far back. Regardless of what was going on personally, I asked if I reported the first time I noticed an error in XXXX, why wasn't there a way to resolve for XXXX disputed transactions. She responded saying they have 30 days to reach a vendor and the time period elapsed to legally do anything. To me, this makes no sense. I asked if there was anything else that can be done? She said nothing. I was frustrated as the reasons provided on this call was the first time I heard of. She said even though she was in authority, she can not speak to why previous customer service associates did not mention these reasons. 

Every single time I have called, I am given a new reason why the claim is disputed and feel I have spent so much time and energy and keep getting kicked around. Now they are saying that they don't have data that goes back XX/XX/XXXX so nothing can be done? Was this the case when I first reported fraud in XX/XX/XXXX. How can BOA not have data of credit card transactions, by law, since XX/XX/XXXX? 

Again, I am yet to see proof of vendor use and I have received ridiculous amounts of hard paper documents saying BOA is unable to approve my recent claim as payments have been made but never showing me proof of the vendor used. 

I feel ridiculous about the amount of energy and time I have dedicated to this case. This has caused me tremendous emotional distress and I hope CFPB can help us reach a resolution. What is the fair way for customers to have fraud claims resolved if the Bank Customer Service are not trained to provide consistent feedback/explanations and guidance on how to resolve a challenge.

_source.complaint_what_happened:
CareCredit through Synchrony Bank was used to finance my hearing aid. My monthly bill was always due on the XXXX. I knew I had until XXXX of 2024, to pay off the balance of {$300.00} as that would be the one year of the interest free promotion. I did not receive a separate email saying this payment would be due on XX/XX/XXXX. I only received an email regarding my normal due date of XX/XX/XXXX.

This practice does not happen with other promotions that I've used for interest free payments plans. In these cases ( XXXX XXXX XXXX ), the due date for the promotion payments stay the same as all previous due dates so the consumer is not blindsided at the end of the promotion. It seems like a deliberate trap by CareCredit to give consumers a different promotion pay off date that is earlier in the month than their typical payment due date. 

The Promotion Terms did not include any dates for the end payment. I did finally find it on the statements on the second page when I looked at them in more depth on XX/XX/XXXX since I was confused about the larger payment due. I find the website to be a bit confusing and difficult to navigate. I did spend more time trying to find out why my payment was higher than expected and finally found the XX/XX/XXXX deadline in smaller print on the second pages of the statements. I don't believe customers should have to search so much for the different date and I feel it is a deliberate practice to create confusion and to trick customers into missing the final promotion due date. 

I received electronic notices of payment due dates for the XXXX of each month. However, no email was sent for the XX/XX/XXXX promotion deadline. I also received an email on XX/XX/XXXX saying my terms had changed. Again, this went to spam and was not seen until just now. It seemed to have good ratings, but I should have been suspicious with any product that claims to be " like magic. '' On their website, they specifically state that there is a money back " risk free '' trial guarantee. Based on this, I felt that it would not hurt to try out the product since, with a money back risk free trial guarantee, it would cost me nothing if the product did not work. The items arrived on XXXX XX/XX/year>, and within a couple days I contacted customer support and notified them that the product was not working, and that the devices were leaking onto my wooden floor and my carpet. They were responsive, and sent out a replacement for some of what I bought. These items did nothing, and released no scent and had no impact on my cats. Instead, I would have to pay return shipping and a {$9.00} fee. I stated this was not what it said on their homepage or in the ads they have everywhere on the internet. They then offered me a XXXX  % refund. I contacted Synchrony bank and disputed the charge as the items were not as described ( they did not work ) and that their money back risk free guarantee actually was false and deceptive. Synchrony bank placed the XXXX charges in dispute and credited my account. I sent to them proof of their advertising as well as the e-mail they sent saying that I it wasn't truly risk free or that I would get my money back. On XXXX XX/XX/year>, Synchrony recharged my account. When I called, I asked if they had received my evidence and I was told no, they had not. _source.complaint_what_happened:
. I am writing to formally address several concerns regarding my Best Buy Citi Card account for the second time, which have not been adequately resolved despite previous attempts to seek clarification. 

1. **Account Closure Without Proper Explanation : ** I received notification that my Best Buy Citi Card account has been closed. This action was taken without any prior warning or explanation provided. I have been a responsible cardholder and have diligently maintained my account in good standing. The abrupt closure of my account has caused significant inconvenience and confusion. 

2. **Unexplained Fees : ** I have recently noticed several charges on my account statement labeled as Interest charges for XXXX purchases. I have not used this card in months but have been charged over XXXX worth of interest charges in the last 5 months. These fees have been applied without any accompanying explanation or breakdown as to their nature or justification. I request a detailed clarification regarding these charges. 

3. **Handling of Dispute Regarding XXXX XXXX XXXX  Transaction : ** I filed a dispute previously concerning a charge from XXXX XXXX XXXX. This charge was supposed to be covered under an insurance claim and should not have been billed to my account. Despite providing supporting documentation, Best Buy Citi Card investigated and denied my dispute, withholding the provisional credit associated with the transaction. This action was unjustified and adversely affected my access to funds. 

4. **Allegations of Retaliation and Discrimination : ** I am concerned that the closure of my account and the mishandling of my dispute may be retaliatory in nature, stemming from a prior complaint I filed with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ). I assert that such actions violate my rights under consumer protection laws, including but not limited to the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( ECOA ), and Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ). 

In light of the above concerns, I hereby request the following actions : - A detailed written explanation regarding the closure of my Best Buy Citi Card account. 
- A comprehensive breakdown and justification for the fees charged to my account. 
- Immediate resolution of the dispute regarding the XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX  transaction, including the release of any withheld provisional credit. 

I trust that Best Buy Citi Card will handle this matter promptly and in accordance with applicable laws and regulations. Please provide a written response addressing the points raised within 30 days of receipt of this letter. 

Should this matter not be resolved satisfactorily, I reserve the right to pursue further action through the appropriate channels, including but not limited to legal remedies and additional complaints to regulatory authorities. 

XXXX XXXX

_source.complaint_what_happened:
I visited the XXXX facility on Sunday, XX/XX/year>. My mother had found an XXXX ad of theirs for relatively cheap XXXX. Immediately during my consultation with a man named XXXX, he insisted that I do not need XXXX - rather a slew of lasers, injections, and fillers to be done over some time. As his face lit up, he exclaimed that he could do a before and after mother/daughter duo for {$120.00}. 
XXXX asked for my driver 's license and social security number, for what I assumed would be to input my information into their system for when we would come back for these future services. My daughter even gave him an old driving license with a previous last name before marriage and the wrong address. Upon further thought, as we were driving home, we both decided that perhaps this was not a good idea, and we should cancel. As soon as XXXX opened on Monday morning, I called the office to let them know that we would not be proceeding. At this point, the woman at the front desk stated that it was too late, but perhaps XXXX could refund half of the money. This is when I realized they had signed me up for a Care Credit card using an expired license with my incorrect last name and incorrect home address. Anything I signed that day was using pre-marriage last name. My daughter has also recently found out that they opened a SECOND credit card in her name with another bank, which she also has to claim identity theft for. It is very clear that this establishment is a scam, and that they use their clients personal information to collect money for no service. Per the Florida Attorney General, In Florida, if you contract for services to be rendered in the future continuingly, you are entitled to a three-day cooling-off period. 
At this point, I have no intention of ever going back to this establishment and am unsure How can they even claim to make me pay for something that I will never get? 
By the way, the guy who supposedly sold us, told me the next day that the owner told him '' Don't worry, this bank always stands with us and never refunds the money to the consumer.

On XX/XX/XXXX my Chase Sapphire Reserve Credit Card account was opened. Without prior notification, the bank closed my account on XX/XX/XXXX. I was surprised because during this time none of my payments were delayed or carried over ( evidence attached ). I never defaulted. To check if the account was closed in error or had a specific reason I called the bank the same day. I was informed that my credit card was closed and that I would receive details about the closure by mail. I was also told that once an account is closed, it can not be reopened. Therefore, I inquired about the annual fee of {$550.00}, which is paid on XX/XX/XXXX each year. The last annual fee was paid on XX/XX/XXXX ( evidence attached ). I was assured that the fee would be prorated and that the remaining amount would be credited back to my credit card account or issued as a check. I was advised to wait for XXXX weeks. 

XXXX weeks later, I received a letter explaining the reason for the account closure and directing me to call a specified number for further details about the fees and balance payments. When I called that number, I was again told that the fee would be prorated in a few weeks and that if I did not see any credit or refund, I should call credit card customer service number. 

After a couple of weeks passed without seeing any credit or check, I called customer service. The agent/supervisor informed me that the annual fee would not be refunded or prorated because it was past 90 days. When I requested an explanation, I was told that the annual fee is only refunded or credited back within 90 days of being charged. I was very surprised by this response. After XXXX weeks of waiting, I received an unfavorable response. I asked if that was specified in the terms and conditions or any policy. She said it is specified in the terms and conditions. I requested the agent to either email or mail me the documents/terms and conditions that clearly state the policy that the annual fee will not be refunded if the card is closed by the bank or specification related to 90 days period. 

I received the documents in the mail ( evidence attached ). Attached is the only document that I received or was sent. After reviewing them, I did not find any clause stating that the annual fee would not be refunded if the card is closed or any other related information. Please feel free to review the same. 

I feel as a customer, it is my right to know of this information and policies. And since it was not provided either on day XXXX or when requested, and therefore it leads to clear misleading and unfair approach. I would like the bank to refund my annual fee of {$550.00}. I am requesting a refund due to misleading information, miscommunication, and the inconvenience caused. A significant amount of time was wasted following up with agents who provided incorrect information and dealing with the hassles of making changes to autopayments that I had set up. 

It is the responsibility of the bank to provide clear terms and conditions for involuntary credit card changes related to fees and/or closing of the account. _source.complaint_what_happened:
On XX/XX/year>, I made a payment to my Prosper credit card online, as I have always done. The payment exceeded the minimum amount due, and the due date was XX/XX/XXXX. On XX/XX/year>, I noticed that the payment had not cleared my bank account. Upon checking my online account, it indicated that the payment was processed on XX/XX/XXXX and that my account was in good standing. 

I contacted Prosper customer service and spoke with representative XXXX. ( Note : All calls are recorded for quality assurance and training purposes. ) XXXX informed me that the payment was returned on XX/XX/year>. When I inquired about the reason, she stated she did not know. I also asked why I was not informed of this, to which she replied that it was not their responsibility. She further stated that I would be charged a returned check fee and a late payment fee. When I expressed my dissatisfaction, she abruptly ended the call. 

I called back and spoke with another representative, XXXX, who informed me that my account was now restricted due to the returned payment and that nothing could be done until I made another payment from a different bank account. Unfortunately, I do not have another bank account. When I asked again why the payment was returned, she said she did not know and that they could not find out. She then ended the call. 

I contacted my bank, XXXX XXXX XXXX, which recently took over XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX on XX/XX/year>. After spending two hours investigating, my bank determined that Prosper, either through their software or manual processing, omitted the first XXXX zeros of my account number, rendering the account unidentifiable and causing the payment to be returned. 

I contacted Prosper again and spoke with representative XXXX, requesting to speak with a manager. She transferred me to a supervisor named XXXX. I explained the situation and my bank 's findings. I made another payment online that same day. XXXX stated that it is their policy to restrict accounts and charge fees regardless of fault. He mentioned he would submit a ticket for investigation but that the fees and restriction would remain. The ticket number is XXXX XXXX 

On XX/XX/year>, I received an email from Prosper stating that they had conducted an investigation and confirmed the payment was returned without providing a reason. They maintained the restrictions and fees, closing the case. I responded, pointing out that my payment was not late until XX/XX/XXXX, so no late fees should apply. The payment was returned due to Prosper 's error in processing my account number. Despite this, they are penalizing me with fees and restrictions. 

In response, Prosper reiterated that the restrictions and fees would remain and closed the case. I informed them that I would be filing a complaint with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau. Representative XXXX then indicated that if I did so, they would close my account and demand immediate full payment of the balance. This response appears to be retaliatory for reporting and refusing to accept responsibility for their actions.

_source.complaint_what_happened:
We have been using Wells Fargo Credit cards for our business since they talked us into using them due to all of the " benefits '' that they would provide. They even talked us into auto payment to make things more convenient. We order XXXX XXXX of dollars per month via the credit card in parts to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. Due to the credit limit on the account we would have to pay the card sometimes XXXX times a month so that we could continue to order parts. This worked great for several years. As we were closing out for the end of the year we kept coming up very short on money and were having a very hard time making payroll for our employees. We kept digging until we found that Fraud had occurred on our credit card over 2 days XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX right after the XXXX. Since this was done over a holiday and in a very short period of 2 days it did not show up amongst all of the other part charges that we had in peak season. The total in credit card XXXX was XXXX done over XXXX transactions in a few different states including Florida and Washington. We immediately turned in the fraud on XX/XX/XXXX. They credited the money back to our card on XX/XX/XXXX and we were able to make payroll. We thought all was well until the charged it all back to our account again on XX/XX/XXXX and started sending denial letters stating that I approved the fraud. We were asked to file a police report and we did that right away and it is attached as well. We have attached many of the denial letters. It seems to be standard procedure to just deny any claim as they did not even know why they were denying the fraud in the beginning. They kept saying that I approved it and it was purchased in person. They then kept asking me If I let anyone else use my card to which I responded, " it is always in my right front pocket and No one uses it but me ''. 
A private investigator named XXXX was assigned to the case and she was able to prove that it was Fraud and has information on how they were committing the crime by using a fake website and selling discounted products that they would in tern purchase with our credit card. XXXX said that the money was all going back to the XXXX XXXX. XXXX phone number is XXXX. XXXX told me on the phone calls that she is 100 % certain that it is fraud, but she said good luck on getting your money back. 
They kept denying the fraud with the attached letters saying that I authorized the purchases and therefore the fraud. After a few denials, they started saying that by me continuing to make payments on the account that I was accepting the fraud. Keep in mind that they talked me into having the account on auto payments and we needed to keep using this card to stay in business as all of our parts are run through this line of credit. This is very frustrating as it is clearly fraud and they are trying everything to not make it right with us. 
We were then assigned another investigator named XXXX and finally, another one named XXXX. XXXX and XXXX also agreed that from the research that they have done that this was clearly fraud and they was hoping it would be taken care of. We have re-opened this case more than 5 times since they keep closing it in attempts to just make it go away. We very much would liked to have seen this fraud sooner than we did, but if diamonds get stolen from a jewelry store and they finally catch the culprit, he has to return the diamonds. 
When we called the places that were in Florida and Washington it was found that the purchases were made over the phone and they did not properly follow procedures to check the credit card or any signatures. This completely blows my mind that someone could make these large purchases over the phone and not even have to sign for them. 99 % of everything purchased on this card came from the same XXXX vendors. I am very disappointed with Wells Fargo for not even questioning these charges as they were all out of state and products and services that we have never purchased before. Please look at the notes and the letters that they keep sending as they never planned on paying back any money on any of this and they were only looking for a way to get out of it from the beginning. _source.complaint_what_happened:
I accepted a Balance Transfer/Check Promotion offer from Barclays, on or around XXXX of XXXX. It was a 0.00 % interest free loan payable on XX/XX/XXXX, it included a 5 % balance transfer fee and the amount of the Balance Transfer/Check Promotion I used was {$20000.00}. 

I received my statement for the month of XXXX, due XX/XX/XXXX, and the total statement balance was {$22000.00} - due XX/XX/XXXX. Which I paid in full on XX/XX/XXXX. I was under the impression that this would satisfy not only my existing charges from the previous month, but also my outstanding loan amount of {$20000.00}. 

It wasn't until I ( thankfully ) called Barclays to confirm my above understanding that I was told some unpleasant and in my opinion rather one-sided, anti-consumer, and for lack of a better term slimy, information. 

Apparently Barclays automatically - there is nothing a consumer can do to alter or affect this - applies the payment, in this case {$22000.00} thusly - to the highest interest baring balances first and then to the lower interest balances last. Well, on the surface that doesn't sound too anti-consumer, but lets take it a step further. 

Barclays in this ( and every other credit card customer of theirs who takes one of these Balance Transfer/Check Promotion offers min you ) case chose to divide my payment thusly - First is satisfies the amount from the past billing cycle - again reasonable ... however here is where it gets slimy, they then satisfy amount of money owed on the CURRENT billing cycle - in other words they take and apply the payment made to an amount which hasn't even come due yet, nor has the current billing cycle 's statement even been generated yet, and then the final leftover amount is applied to the 0.0 % Balance Transfer/Check Promotion offer balance of {$20000.00}. 

If I had not have called to verify that I had met my obligations on the {$20000.00} Balance Transfer/Check Promotion offer , then I would have never known this, and I would have had an outstanding balance with ~14 months worth of interest of about {$2100.00} ( the amount of charges I had made on the current biling cycle that again hadn't even closed nor a statement been generated for me to pay yet, or in other terms I was still within the grace period. 

This is in my opinion unconscionable and wrong, while those charges I had yet to be billed for would ( eventually ) indeed have a normal 21 % APR, they shoud not in my perspective be absorbing any of my payment, because those charges have not even been billed to me yet, this feels absolutely and entirely preditory in nature and I believe this practice ought to be either outlawed, or a consumer should have the right to allocate their payment as they chose, not as Barclays not only defaults to, but when I called I was told there was NO ONE at Barclays who could amend the allocation of my payment. They have chosen how to apply my payment in a way that benefits them, and only them, and it is clearly not in the consumers best interest. 

I have now had to pay {$2100.00}, more than what my current stated balance is, because I also have pending charges from recently using my card today, that I have to make sure I cover those sums as well to avoid paying interest.

_source.complaint_what_happened:
In summary, due to a newborn arrival, I got 1 day delayed in a full statement payment, resulting in only partial payment for that month. The amount left over was about {$1000.00}, which was paid in full the next day in addition to all other balances in my account. In the following 2 months, I got surprised by about {$79.00} in charges, which is an absurd APR ( {$79.00} for 1 day! ). 

Upon discussion with customer service, they finally admited to weird and likely unlawful practices of charging interest for at least 2 months, irrespective whether I paid the bill the next day or not. In addition, any new charges to the credit card was " game '' for them to charge me more interest, which were transactions not even billed yet, so there was no way I would have known I was paying interest on them and would otherwise have long dropped this credit card to begin with. 

This is effectively charging interest on purchases that have not made into a statement yet, giving the consumer the wrong impression of how a credit card should work. Had I known they would keep charging me interest on any balance on the card, including current in progress cycle, I would have stopped used this credit card immediately. I clearly had the funds to do so, as you can see on the timeline attached, I just missed 1 day of payment. Overall, this seems malpractice, a sort of scam to charge more interest, completely diminishing the trust in this financial system, and potentially causing imense hardship for customers that are already struggling to pay their bills. This seems illegal to me and should likely be reviewed by the State Attorney 's General Office and be target for Class action suits, since it might be impacting millions of Americans trying to stay afloat in the economy. This ultimately makes their bills unbearable to pay for if they don't have the means. 

This agency should review these practices and decide whether this is legitimate type of interaction and whether it's not an abuse of consumers ' trust.

_source.complaint_what_happened:
On XX/XX/2024, my billing cycle closed, and I had a balance of {$9600.00}, with a due date of XX/XX/2024 ( see attachment ). By that date, I had made partial payments and redeemed reward credits totaling {$10000.00}. Regardless, on XX/XX/2024, Capital One made a withdrawal from my checking account through their " Auto Pay '' system for {$8200.00}. This was improper because the total credits applied to my account exceeded the balance due on that date, so I disputed the transaction with my bank, and the payment was returned. 

Capital One now claims that despite the fact that the total credits applied to my account exceeded the balance due by XX/XX/XXXX, I did not make the total payment due, and my account is past due. While I fully disagree with their contention that my account was ever past due, I agreed to make a payment of {$1000.00} today ( XX/XX/2024 ). Capital One 's representative XXXX, ID number XXXX, promised that if this payment was made today, no information about a past due payment, or anything other than " paid as agreed '' would be reported to credit bureaus. While I was skeptical of this promise, I agreed to make the payment, in the interest of protecting my credit rating. 

After extensive discussions with Capital One, the dispute boils down to the application of two Capital One policies, which I contend are misleading and improper : 1. Capital One 's Auto Pay feature allows a consumer to automatically schedule a payment to pay statement balances in full on the due date. However, nonsensically ( and in opposition to the behavior most of their competitors ), Capital One does not subtract any early payments made from the " balance '' due. Capital One representatives have described this to me as " that's just the way Auto Pay works, '' and claimed that in order to truly have only the balance due subtracted, I would have to call the company before any automatic payments are completed. The behavior of their Auto Pay is both unreasonable, and opposite to how the system is described on their own website when setting up the feature ( see attached image ). Applying a common sense interpretation of what a consumer would believe will happen is not congruent with the behavior of their system. 

2. Capital One does not apply promotional credits to payments due, and does not make it clear to the consumer that this behavior exists. All promotional credits are listed as payments on their website and their statements ( see attachment ), like any other payment would appear. Despite this, Capital One does not apply these credits at the time they are redeemed, but holds the credits and applies them to the balance due at the end of the billing cycle - despite the fact that they appear immediately on the transaction list, with the redemption date. Given the way the information is presented by Capital One, any consumer would be expected to believe that their credits had been applied to their account immediately.

According to 15 U.S.C. 1691, the ECOA prohibits discrimination against applicants on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, sex, marital status, age ( provided the applicant has the capacity to contract ), or because all or part of the applicant 's income derives from any public assistance program, or because the applicant has in good faith exercised any right under the Consumer Credit Protection Act.

Furthermore, the issuance of an Adverse Action Letter in place of the credit extension is an unauthorized use of my credit information.

I am requesting the following actions be taken : A detailed written explanation for the denial of my credit application.

An investigation into whether any discriminatory practices occurred during the processing of my application.

A reassessment of my credit application to ensure it is evaluated fairly and in compliance with the ECOA.

I trust that Costco Wholesale Corporation and Citibank , N.A . will take this matter seriously and respond promptly to my concerns. Please provide the requested information and any relevant findings within 30 days of receipt of this letter.

Thank you for your attention to this matter. I look forward to your prompt and thorough response.

_source.complaint_what_happened:
I am attempting to reconcile the charge account bill ( which I have always pay in full each month since obtaining the card several years ago - as evidenced by never having paid a cent in interest charges ). To do so, I signed on to my account, where it clearly says 3 months of statements are provided on-line, yet I can only access 1 month of statement, it is like nothing existed prior to this last month. 

I contacted the Kohls Credit Card by phone and asked for assistance. They told me that I did not have access to the online statements because they do not provide that to customers who receive HARD COPY STATEMENTS. They told me if I wanted to have access to prior months on-line, I would have to sign up for PAPERLESS STATEMENTS. 

I carefully read all the disclosures and policies and procedures available on Kohl 's web site including the eye test of disclosures mailed to me the last time they mailed out updated XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXs, no where do they describe a relationship between PAPERLESS STATEMENTS and the ability to examine the last 3 months of statements on-line. 

I have never seen or heard of services being withheld on the basis of having or not having selected Paperless Statements- especially without ever disclosing same to consumers when they make the choice. 

I do not believe that Kohl 's have the right to selectively withhold on-line access services from an account in good standing without disclosing same to customers. 

Because I was performing this analysis while on an extended vacation away from home, I had no ability to look at the paper statements I had at home. After speaking with the customer rep who assured me that access would be provided after I signed up for paperless billing, I did so, in pursuit of tracking down the issue I was attempting to understand. 

Ha. After signing up, I still was not given access to the 3 months of statements. I did that about 20 days ago. Then suddenly, in the last few days ONLY the statement which was produced a week ago was available to be seen. So, after all of that, I was still prevented from accessing the information I needed. 

I do not believe it is fair for Kohl 's Charge Card to withhold access without disclosure that describes the details of what will be withheld, and the fact it would then take 90 days before the full 90 days of statements would become available on-line. 

After all of that, I am still unable to reconcile the account and evidently will not be able to do so until another 60 days pass, or I return home. Ludicrous! 

More ridiculous, the Customer Service Rep at Kohl 's claimed that they too did not have access to the statements in question until I signed up for Paperless Statements, and 90 days passed for the statements to " age onto the system ''. 

We all know that is ridiculous. Of course they must have access to the statement history. And yes, they had to have paid programmers to withhold access to statements by the customer AND THE CSR 'S unless the CSR outright lied to me- which I am unwilling to claim. I have to proceed on the basis they told me the truth. 

In summary : I do not believe Kohl 's Card can reasonably withhold access to 90 days of customer statements because they wish me to sign up for some service they want me to utilize - whether or not if it saves them money. This is a slippery slope for for-profit financial services companies. If not stopped now from creating a defacto fee for service that prevents the customer from accessing information they need ( and which the company must supply to customers and their CSR staff ), in a world where self-service has become the norm and Customer Support is virtually non-existent already powered by AI engines unable to respond to any issue that extends beyond it's purview- the customer is left without support or access to information they require. 

Financial services firms lead the world in eliminating living-breathing-agents with whom a consumer can contact to resolve issues that have complexity above a 90 IQ - which is the target intelligence for an AI engine. This is one of the reasons CFPB was created. Financial Services requires more oversight than a grocery store - and have the automation to manipulate ignorant consumers who are clueless as to their rights. 

Please remember, these are basic Bill & Receipt revolving Charge Accounts for a mid-sized department store. However, in reality, department stores outsource their Private Label Charge Card to large Financial Service Providers that test new concepts in this smaller test market well below the eye 's or regulators. This is a glimpse into the future for a largely de-regulated industry that has grown into the Trillions in the past 10 years with payday lenders et al who now are owned by the most " reputable '' financial services firms, who all charge usury interests rates exported from states who repealed all usury laws in favor of attracting more business to their state. 

The consumer has been and continues to be the loser in this future of self regulation. Please draw the lines as firmly as possible every chance you get. 

Sincerely, XXXX XXXX

_source.complaint_what_happened:
This is in reference to case number XXXX. The response I received was unsatisfactory and violates several key provisions outlined in federal law, including the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) and the CFPB Complaint Process. I'm asking this get removed from my credit report and the CFPB does their due diligence. 

Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( 15 U.S. Code 1681s-2 ( b ) ), furnishers of information to credit bureaus, such as XXXX and TD Retail Card Services, are required to investigate disputes and provide evidence to the consumer if their investigation finds that the disputed information is accurate. Moreover, the CFPB Complaint Process mandates that when a complaint is filed, the company must respond and provide supporting documents to both the CFPB and the consumer. This includes addressing specific allegations made by the consumer, such as the failure to send payment notifications. 

Despite these requirements, I have received no supporting documents or evidence that the disputed information was accurate. Below is my second letter to TD Retail Card Services, which explicitly calls out the statutes and regulations governing the response and documentation requirements.

_source.complaint_what_happened:
On XX/XX/year>, I was in XXXX XXXX, XXXX on vacation. I ate at a restaurant where two men approached me, claiming to be employees. I asked for a menu, but they said there wasn't one and asked what I wanted. I ordered shrimp with rice and a passionfruit juice. When I tried to pay with my US Bank XXXX credit card, they said their system was down and we needed to go to a nearby merchant to process the payment. 

On XX/XX/year>, I discovered they had charged me {$300.00} for the meal. Assuming it was an overcharge, I submitted a dispute to US Bank. They categorized it as a mistaken overcharge and sent paperwork for me to complete. After filing the dispute, I researched and found this was a common scam at that beach. 

I collected news articles and trip reviews about similar scams and submitted this information to US Bank on XX/XX/year> ( file attached ). 

On XX/XX/XXXX, the charges reappeared on my account, so I called US Bank. The representative asked if I had received a resolution letter, which I had not. She said the charge would be credited back, but it never was. 

On XX/XX/year>, I received a letter stating my dispute was denied due to insufficient information ( file attached ). I called US Bank again and was told they would request to reopen the case and recategorize it from incorrect amount to fraud. However, nothing happened, and the charge remained, accruing interest. 

I followed up on XX/XX/year>, and was told the case had not been reopened or refiled correctly, but another request would be made. 

On XX/XX/year>, I called again and found the case still hadn't been properly handled and was still not reopened/recategorized. I spoke to a customer service supervisor who explained : 1. Dispute representatives can not remove charges or reopen cases ; they can only request case managers to do so. This had not been explained to me, so I thought my case was being processed.

2. Case managers can't receive inbound calls, even from dispute representatives ; requests are submitted electronically and no follow up information is available to the dispute representatives.

3.I would have 
to wait for a call back from a case manager supervisor. Previous call attempts were made when I couldn't answer, and no messages were left. I explained that as a full-time worker and student, I can't always answer calls. The representative told me to prioritize the call but could only give a window, not an exact time.

I am stuck in a loop of inaccurate information, dead ends, red tape, and dysfunctional processes. I feel US Bank allowed me to be scammed, and I plan to end my business with them. I recommend the CFPB investigate this and advise consumers to avoid their financial products.

Subject : XXXX XXXX XXXX Navy Federal Credit Union for Premature Dispute Resolution Closure To Whom It May Concern at the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, I am writing to file a formal complaint against Navy Federal Credit Union regarding their handling of my credit card dispute claims. The claims in question concern XXXX transactions made with XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX, XXXX for {$6200.00} and another for {$380.00}, which were both summarily dismissed by the credit union on XX/XX/XXXX. 

Details of the Dispute : The purchases at XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX were conducted under circumstances involving misleading sales tactics and high-pressure sales environments, which I believe misrepresented the nature and value of the services and products offered. Despite my efforts to amicably resolve the issues with the merchant, including attempts to return the unopened merchandise, I was met with non-responsiveness. Subsequently, I turned to Navy Federal Credit Union for assistance. 

Concerns with Navy Federal 's Resolution Process : The decisions to close my claims were based solely on the premise that I received merchandise or a service in exchange for the payment. This overlooks the core issues of my dispute : the deceptive practices employed during the sale. Navy Federal 's investigation concluded without a proper review of the detailed evidence I provided, which documented the circumstances of the sales and my attempts to rectify the situation directly with the merchant. 

Inadequate XXXX and XXXX Rights : I am concerned that the swift closure of my disputes suggests an inadequate review of the facts and fails to uphold my rights as a consumer. According to the XXXX Credit Billing Act, consumers are entitled to a fair investigation of their disputes, and creditors are required to consider all evidence presented by the consumer. The rapid dismissal of my disputes appears to contravene these requirements, leaving me without recourse against practices that I believe are unfair and deceptive. 

Request for CFPB Intervention : Given the issues outlined, I am seeking the CFPBs intervention to ensure a thorough and fair reevaluation of these disputes by Navy Federal Credit Union. It is imperative that financial institutions adhere to regulatory standards that protect consumers from fraudulent and deceptive business practices.

Truist sent a letter to let me know that I have lost my promotional offer rate on my business credit card account ending in XXXX. 

The Truth in Lending Act, primarily codified at 15 U.S. Code 1601 and following, aims to promote informed use of consumer credit by requiring disclosures about its terms and cost.

Under TILA, lenders must clearly disclose the terms and costs of credit. This includes the APR, finance charges, amount financed, and total payments.

15 U.S. Code 1637 outlines the disclosure requirements for open-end consumer credit plans ( like credit cards ).

TILA also addresses changes in terms for credit accounts.

15 U.S. Code 1637 ( i ) requires creditors to provide a 45-day advance notice before increasing the APR or making other significant changes to the terms of a credit card account. This allows consumers time to opt-out of the changes if they choose.

Additional Protections The Credit CARD Act of 2009, which amended TILA, provides further protections : Credit card issuers must generally provide 45 days notice before increasing the interest rate on an existing balance.

Promotional rates must last for at least six months.

I applied for a loan to purchase a computer. After receiving the laptop, I paid the entire bill without any issues. However, I later began receiving bills for {$7.00} for an account I never signed up for. I contacted the company, and they assured me they would remove the amount and close the account. Although they closed the account as promised, they continued to send me bills and added the amount to my credit report. The bill has now increased to {$77.00} due to growing late fees. I disputed the account, but the three reporting agencies claimed it was accurate. I was unaware of the existence of this secondary account. The company should have disclosed this information to me. I would have informed them that I did not require the additional services if they had. The purchase came with a warranty. My sole intention was to purchase a computer. I urgently need assistance removing this incorrect information from my credit report, as it shows that I was late in paying a bill that I was unaware of.

I request the removal of three late payments from all three credit reporting bureaus. Additionally, I was unaware of the service fee after the contract ended and would like it to be eliminated. I also request that the service be stopped from accruing any more late payments. If the service were included in my contract, I would like it to stop once the contract is paid in full. They should send a letter or email confirming that the service will stop once the computer is paid in full and allow me to opt for an extension if I choose to continue the services. The service is hidden in the contract with the loan of the service, and I would like more transparency in this matter.

_source.complaint_what_happened:
In XXXX of XXXX I enrolled in Citibank 's Merchant Offer with XXXX for 6 % cash back on online purchases through XXXX. On XX/XX/XXXX I made a purchase on XXXX for {$7500.00}, expecting that I would receive a credit in the amount of {$450.00}. After I received my first statement, I noticed that I had not been given the credit on my account. I contacted Citibank and inquired when the credit would be posted. They advised it can take up to 8 weeks for the credit to show up. Therefore, when the 8 weeks passed, and I still had not received the credit, I called back. The Representative said she would look into and send a note to the department to check on the status. Each week I would log into my account to see if the credit posted, it did not. I have called Citibank over 18x regarding the status of the credit. Each time I have to explain the situation to a representative who then will transfer me to a manager in the " back office ''. I have spoken to multiple managers who advised that my concerns have been noted and that they will follow up. Some managers advised they would call me back and do not. Some managers would hang up on me, knowing that I would not speak with them if I called back. It has been four months since I made the purchase, and the credit still has not been posted to my account. I have paid off each statement balance. 

Unfortunately, I now feel that this is a scam. The Citibank Merchant Offers are there for you to think you will get a credit, which never comes to fruition. If you call into inquire about the credit, they continue to say someone is taking care of it and never does. Eventually thinking the consumer will give up due to frustration.

I am submitting this complaint as I do not feel that Citibank is addressing my issue and the only way they will is elevating it to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau. Please feel free to contact me to discuss this situation further. 

Regards, XXXX XXXX

_source.complaint_what_happened:
About three months ago I opened a checking account with Capital One Bank, and for this purpose and management of my account I downloaded their application. After a few days, in the application a pre-approved for the capital one quick silver card appeared ( I did not see anywhere under what conditions ), which I clicked on and it simply directed me to the page where they requested additional information, ( social number, tax, and other things that I don't remember ), carry out this procedure and put the entry request on hold. After 24 hours I received an email telling me that my Quick Silver card was approved and that it would be sent in the next few days. In that email, no mention was ever made of the conditions under which it was approved. However, due to the negligence of the bank or the delivery service, I received that card almost a month later ( I even had to request a replacement card ). 
Now the problem is stipulated in the misleading advertising of this bank with its Quick Silver franchise, when one enters the Internet or XXXX search engine one sees the benefits of this card, among which are a bonus of XXXX dollars if I spend XXXX dollars during the First 3 months, this benefit is very common on credit cards, so much so that on my two XXXX  XXXX XXXX credit cards, you receive this benefit without any problem. 
but not this bank and its deceptions ... today, XX/XX/year>, I came to find out that these characters handle 4 types of Quick Silver cards and that according to them the one they approved for me does not have this benefit, something really outrageous and that It bothers me quite a bit. If they informed me of conditions in the approval email, I don't remember it and unfortunately I deleted that email, now under the light of the law, do they inform me of that after approving it? It would be too late to reject it, right? Approved is approved and even my credit report will be affected, something that never happened with my other bank. 

Now why don't they get cards with different names? No, they take advantage of this so that naive people like me fall into their trap. The truth is, I decided to open this card for the welcome bonus, not for more, since I have two credit cards from another bank, which I rarely use., and with the quota I have it is more than enough for me. 
I want this problem to be thoroughly investigated because we are in the light of misleading advertising, as I told you, on my portal only quick silver credit cards appeared ... but the profiteers differentiate between those that have the benefit of the bonus and those that have the benefit of the bonus. not with the following names or terms Quick silver rewards credit excellent and quick silver rewards credit good.. how is this possible? I know many people have fallen for this scam. 
Now, they manage a referral program, to which when you refer, you do it for the same card that you have, right? I referred my wife who has more or less the same credit score as mine, and when they approved her and he spent his XXXX dollars if they gave him that benefit. 
The truth is that what that bank is doing with its clients is a pretty serious deception, and even more so with the misleading advertising that appears in internet search engines and that comes from the official Capital One website. Please investigate, I'm not doing this for XXXX dollars, that's not going to make me richer, I'm doing it so that more people don't fall for this dirty trick. 
thank you so much.

_source.complaint_what_happened:
The card offers XXXX kinds of promotional deferred interest plans : " XXXX equal monthly payments '' with deferred interest where you pay amount borrowed off with XXXX equal payments in XXXX  months and no interest will be charged, " Deferred interest with payment '' where you can pay any amount each month and as long as you make the necessary minimal monthly payment and the total is paid off in XXXX months no interest will be charged, and non-promotional or standard interest terms where you have to pay the balance in full each month in order to avoid an interest charge.. 

My intention when using any credit card is to manage my payments so that I avoid paying interest on the amount of money I put on the card regardless of the terms that apply to the purchase. The credit cards goal is for me to pay them interest. Knowing how much to pay each month to avoid interest is crucial information for a consumer to have and it is in the interest of the credit card company to make this information hard to know, how to find on the statement and how to figure out if it isn't clearly stated. 

I have other credit cards with other credit card companies that offer the same kind of credit use. Those companies make it very clear and easy to know how much I need to pay to avoid interest charges for each monthly statement cycle. They have it listed on very clearly on the front and top of the statement. It is labeled " Amount to pay to avoid interest ''. This is very clear and aboveboard and there is no deception involved, no making it hard for the consumer to figure out. You don't have to search through pages of data or do any math calculations to know what to pay to avoid interest. 

This company on the other hand, does not tell you up front and in an easy, clear way how much you need to pay to avoid interest charges. The information you need to figure it out is scattered all over the multiple pages and sections of the statement. 

Another way they make it confusing and unclear is that they use the word " Regular '' to describe the amount of current balance charges that will accrue interest if not paid in full. They use the words " XXXX equal monthly payments XXXX XXXX interest '' to describe the promotional rate purchase amounts. These amounts are in a running list, not in separate lists or boxes and it is hard to miss seeing the distinction when you look at the statement. 

The most complicated way they make it difficult is that you end up having to find and uses XXXX or XXXX amounts and you have to do some math with them to figure out the minimum payment necessary to avoid a monthly interest charge. 

On the front page of the statement they put the current balance. Turns out this includes each kind of promotional and the non- promotional totals. There is no separating out offered. 

On page XXXX there is the long ( if you use the card a lot ) list of different kinds of balances, regular ( their term ), XXXX equal payments, and deferred interest. If XXXX looks hard enough you can find the total for each category. 

At that point you have to take the total balance and subtract the " regular '' amount. Then if there is a deferred interest amount, I guess you would subtract that too, then you are left with the amount of XXXX equal payment and you have to divide that by XXXX to find the necessary amount to pay. Then you add the regular, the XXXX months back up and throw in the amount you want to pay on the XXXX months deferred interest amount to be sure you pay it off in time. This is a lot of math work and studying of the statement to find the info you need for your calculation! 

Finally, the customer service person I talked to tried to explain to me how they determine how to apply the payment you send them, which category they apply it to first. But by then my head was still trying to wrap my head around how to find info and what math to do. 

My point is that by making the statement and process so multi-step and complicated, it adds up to being on the verge of deceptive! I am angry because I have ended up paying interest almost every month, or at least the last XXXX months of statements I looked at to check back and see. When I asked myself " How did this happen?! '' and called customer service to ask about it and learned how complicated it was, I felt cheated and taken advantage of ... tricked! Or at least compared to other credit card companies like the XXXX XXXX XXXX card I have that very simply puts right on the front of my statement in LARGE print, " Amount to pay to avoid interest ''. Haven't paid any interest to them in years! 

I don't expect to get all that interest back from Synchrony. I am making this complaint so that you can look into the way they do their statement and maybe help others avoid their deceptive little game. I plan to pay off my full balance and never use the card again. I will never accept or use any other card that comes from Synchrony. I will write to Amazon and suggest they change the bank that manages their store card. I also have a JCPenny store card, a PayPal XXXX and Lowes card managed by Synchrony that I will never use again and will write to those companies as well. Synchrony is sleazy. Oh I'm sure they are technically legal but their practices are deceptive as in unnecessarily ( an in my opinion ) purposely complicated. Sure, I can see them saying, " If it's to hard, don't use the card. '' and that is exactly what I plan to do! 

I won't close the accounts since I know that dings XXXX 's credit rating, just stash the cards and never touch them again, and tell everyone I know to never accept a credit card that involves Synchrony. Thank you for your attention to my concerns. Please do what you can to change how Synchrony does it's business.

_source.complaint_what_happened:
I lost my job just before Covid, then had trouble finding a new one due to the pandemic, so for about 5 months I could not pay my bills. My account with the card issuer was closed as a charge off with a balance due. I have since regained employment and paid back my creditors, except for two. One is on a payment plan and this one will not accept my money. 

After reaching out to them to either settle my account for less or be on a payment plan to pay the balance back in full, I was told that the debt had been canceled and I was issued a 1099C. Its possible I received one, though I can not recall ; however, this creditor is still reporting the full balance due monthly to the three major credit bureaus. If the debt was indeed cancelled, my balance due should be reported as {$0.00} and if it wasnt cancelled, then I should be given the opportunity to repay the debt. 

This unfair practice of the original creditor to not allow me to pay and continue to report a balance every month on my credit report, thus tanking my score, is making it nearly impossible to purchase a home or obtain new credit.

DOUBLE REWARDS : Earn 10 % back across XXXX brands for your first 30 days. '' I then returned to the same Pottery Barn store on XX/XX/year> and worked with the same Designer in store to place an order for all of my furniture on the same day. I, together with the Designer, ended up placing an online order with Pottery Barn in the amount of {$24000.00}, an online order with XXXX XXXX in the amount of {$440.00}, and also made an in store purchase with Pottery Barn in the amount of {$470.00}. To reiterate, all the purchases were made on XX/XX/year>, well within the first 30 days of applying for the Pottery Barn Key Rewards Visa, and paid for by my new Pottery Barn Key Rewards Visa. Since then, all of the aforementioned charges have been posted to my Capital One Pottery Barn Key Rewards Visa totaling {$21000.00} from the online Pottery Barn order and {$470.00} for the in store Pottery Barn purchase, and I have paid off all of these charges in full. The only charges that are yet to be posted include a backordered item from Pottery Barn in the amount of {$1100.00} and the XXXX XXXX order in the amount {$440.00}. I have also subsequently canceled one item from the online Pottery Barn order since it was backordered, but the charges for that item never posted. To summarize, Pottery Barn has charged a total of {$22000.00} to my Capital One Pottery Barn Key Rewards Visa to date, so I was expecting to receive 10 % back in Key Rewards, amounting to {$2200.00} since the entire order was placed within 30 days of applying for the Capital One Pottery Barn Key Rewards Visa. This does not include the charges for the backordered item from Pottery Barn in the amount of {$1100.00} and the XXXX XXXX order in the amount {$440.00} that are yet to be posted, even though they were paid for on XX/XX/year> so I am expecting 10 % back on those as well. However, I have only received {$1100.00} back in Key Rewards to date, which is closer to 5 % back rather than the advertised and promised 10 % back, and the aforementioned cash back also includes rewards on {$1900.00} in other purchases that I have made on groceries and restaurants that would have given me {$79.00} in cash back at the 4 % back rate for these categories. In conclusion, Pottery Barn and Capital One still owe me approximately {$1100.00} in Key Rewards for the Pottery Barn charges totaling {$22000.00} that were posted to my Capital One Pottery Barn Key Rewards Visa to date. _source.complaint_what_happened:
I have been a loyal customer of Capital One for an extensive period, diligently ensuring that my payments are made on time and even exceeding the minimum required amount. However, in XXXX, I encountered an unforeseen issue when a payment I submitted was returned due to a shortage in funds caused by my mortgage company charging my mortgage. To rectify the situation, I promptly made a second payment of {$700.00}. Surprisingly, Capital One did not attempt to withdraw this payment from my checking account. Perplexed, I logged into my account after two days and, realizing that the payment was not processed, I decided to submit an additional {$500.00} payment. Unfortunately, the same issue persisted three times consecutively.

Frustrated by the lack of progress, I contacted Capital One and was fortunate enough to speak with a supervisor who agreed to conference call XXXX XXXX, my banking institution. During the call, XXXX XXXX confirmed that Capital One had indeed failed to initiate the payment attempts following the incident in XXXX. This failure occurred on three separate occasions. After making a second call to seek resolution, an agent informed me that I could make a payment over the phone without incurring any charges. However, I opted to make the payment through the app, as I had verified that I had sufficient funds in my account. The agent assured me that the payment would be reflected by the following day, and we concluded the call. 

The next morning, I logged into my Capital One account to ensure that everything was in order, only to discover that my account had been closed due to the aforementioned situation. This outcome is entirely unacceptable, considering that Capital One was at fault, not me. 

I maintained a flawless payment history with Capital One, yet their system experienced a glitch that resulted in the failure to request payments. Furthermore, during one instance, I had Capital One on the line while we contacted XXXX XXXX, who confirmed that no attempts were made to retrieve the payment. 

It is disheartening that Capital One chose to close my account without attempting to resolve the issue, especially considering my long-standing record of timely payments. Even with my account closed, they continue to accumulate debt, which is entirely unacceptable.

I was taken aback, because my first thought was that I had just gotten a new store credit card, also a XXXX, so that maybe this had to do with that card. There is no contact information listed on this letter ; only a website to where I can upload the " missing '' information. When I finally was able to find a number on the internet and get a person on the phone, he politely declared to me that " this was just an advertisement. '' The letter, paraphrased, states, " Thank you for applying... we need the following information to continue processing, within the next 30 days. '' No where in the letter or in it's fine print, is it made clear that this is an advertisement or marketing attempt to enroll someone to a new account.

I am writing to formally request the removal of an unauthorized inquiry by Bank of America from my XXXX credit report. This inquiry was conducted without my consent, which is a violation of my rights under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), specifically under 15 U.S.C. 1681b ( a ) ( 2 ). 

Details of the Unauthorized Inquiry : Company Name : Bank of America Date of Inquiry : XX/XX/year> Credit Reporting Agency : XXXX Legal Basis for the Request : According to 15 U.S.C. 1681b ( a ) ( 2 ), a consumer reporting agency may only furnish a consumer report if it is " in accordance with the written instructions of the consumer to whom it relates. '' I have not provided any written instructions or consent for Bank of America to conduct a credit inquiry on my XXXX report. This unauthorized inquiry violates my rights under the FCRA.

Additionally, 15 U.S.C. 1681c ( a ) ( 1 ) mandates that inaccurate or unverifiable information must be removed from a consumer report. Since this inquiry was neither authorized by me nor conducted for a legitimate purpose, it qualifies as erroneous information and should be removed immediately. 

Impact of the Unauthorized Inquiry : The unauthorized inquiry by Bank of America has negatively impacted my credit score and overall creditworthiness. It reflects incorrect and misleading information on my credit report, which can hinder my ability to secure credit and other financial services. 

Requested Action : I am requesting that the CFPB investigate this unauthorized inquiry and ensure its prompt removal from my XXXX credit report. This action will help correct the inaccuracy on my report and mitigate any further adverse effects on my financial standing.
