_source.complaint_what_happened:
I am writing to submit a complaint regarding a promotional balance transfer offer that I received as a credit card account holder at Bank of America. 

Here is a timeline : On XX/XX/XXXX a direct deposit was made from my available credit to my bank account in the amount of {$7600.00}. At this time I was also charged a transaction fee of {$300.00}. Note that I already had an existing balance on this card, which was {$2700.00} at the end of XX/XX/XXXX. 

The promotional offer ID was : XXXX. 

The end date for this promotional rate was on XX/XX/XXXX. 

For approximately one year ( XXXX XXXX XXXX ) I made the minimum monthly payments on this account. Because these payments went toward the lowest APR balances first as is stated in Bank of Americas account information on the monthly statements, my payments as I understand went toward paying off the direct deposit balance. 

On XX/XX/XXXX I received an email from Bank of America with the subject line : Your credit card promotional rate expires soon. ( Note that I have attached this email for reference. ) Nowhere in this email were there any specific instructions for how to pay off the balance with the promotional APR when the account had another balance with another APR. There was only the note to Log in to monitor your balance ( s ) or make payments. 

On XX/XX/XXXX I made a large payment of {$6000.00} on this account. In the XX/XX/XXXX- XX/XX/XXXX statement this was the balance amount listed as subject to the promotional interest rate. I wanted to make sure that I made this payment well in advance of the promotional end date to avoid having a large balance with a very high interest rate. I used a little under half of my modest divorce settlement to make this payment. 

Because I used my credit card attached to this account very little until spring of this year, I only recently took a thorough look at my latest statements and realized to my great dismay that the promotional balance that I thought I had paid off is now growing by the month (!! ) and Im paying a hefty interest rate each month. This situation is exactly what I wanted to avoid!!! To make matters worse, Im now in a very tight financial position where I can only make the minimum monthly payments. 

I called Bank of America on XX/XX/XXXX and spoke with two associates and the supervisor of one of these associates. ( Note I had to end the first call as it was just about to run into an important meeting that I had scheduled. ) The second time I called the associate connected me to their supervisor. 

All the Bank of America representatives quickly grasped the problem, yet I got very different answers on what I should have done about it. One of the representatives told me that I should have made the minimum monthly payment in XXXX on top of the payment I submitted to clear my direct deposit balance. 

Later, another representative kept reading me the fine print in the account statement, which felt demeaning to me. I understood the fine print, yet did not understand how I should have coordinated my big payment to avoid the current mess in which I find myself. 

I was finally told that I should have made that payment on XX/XX/XXXX. Yet, nowhere was that made clear. From my standpoint it would not have made sense to wait until the XXXX and risk and risk being hit with a huge interest fee. Ive taken advantage of XXXX APR financing in the past with other companies to finance medical debt and Ive always been extraordinarily careful about paying off those balances to avoid the extremely high interest charges that kick in right after a promotional period ends. 

Yet, in this case, despite acting in good faith to pay off my promotional balance in full and on time, I am now paying dearly and will continue to do so on a balance with a very high APR that is growing by the month. And, this situation is unfolding at a time when I can barely afford to put food on the table. 

This situation feels incredibly unfair to the point of being predatory, especially given the confusing messages from Bank of Americas own representatives and vague written correspondence from the bank. 

Thank you so much for your attention to this troubling matter!

_source.complaint_what_happened:
XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, IL, XXXX XXXX XXXX **Barclays Card Services** XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, DE XXXX XXXXSubject : Good Faith Letter for Reconsideration and Conditional Acceptance** To whom it may concern at Barclays Card Services, I'm writing to have my application for the XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX Credit Card reconsidered in accordance with 15 U.S. Code 1691. It shall be unlawful for any creditor to discriminate against any applicant, with respect to any aspect of a credit transaction because the applicant has in good faith exercised any right under this chapter.

I exercised my RIGHT to credit in good faith and I did not expect my application to be denied. This decision not only adversely affects me but also, I believe, constitutes a violation of federal laws in place to protect applicants like myself. In accordance with 15 U.S. Code 1691 ( d ) adverse action defined ( 6 ), the term adverse action does not include a refusal to extend additional credit under an existing credit arrangement where such additional credit would exceed a previously established credit limit. So I can not be denied credit simply from adverse action.

In accordance with 15 U.S. Code 1602 ( f ), the term credit means the RIGHT granted by a creditor to a debtor to incur debt and defer its payment. I, XXXX XXXX, do not need to defer any payments but I did exercise my right to incur debt. Pursuant to 15 U.S. Code 1691a ( b ), the term applicant means any person who applies to a creditor indirectly by use of an existing credit plan for an amount exceeding a previously established credit limit.

You might be wondering what is this credit plan? Well, it's defined in 15 U.S. Code 1602 ( j ) : A credit plan or open-end consumer credit plan which is an open-end credit plan or open-end consumer credit plan within the meaning of the preceding sentence is an open-end credit plan. So for something to be open-ended, it simply means unlimited. I have the lawful right to extend credit unlimitedly to incur debt so long as I operate at peace as well as in good faith. 

I, XXXX XXXX, am more than able, capable, and willing to pay back any credit extended to me. I only applied for this credit card to start a new financial relationship with Barclays Card Services. No other company could fit my needs from what I've researched, and I thank you for taking my application as well as this letter into consideration when someone takes a second look at my application. 

In accordance with 12 CFR Part 1002 - Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( Regulation B ), Regulation B protects applicants from discrimination in any aspect of a credit transaction. Credit transactions and aspects of credit transactions include, but are not limited to, consumer credit, business credit, open-end credit, credit applications, standards of creditworthiness, denial of credit, revocation, or termination of credit.

In accordance with 15 U.S. Code 1642 - Issuance of credit cards, no credit card shall be issued except in response to a request or application therefor. I made a request and no fiduciary obligation was upheld by Barclays Card Services.

I will only accept your offer to deny me credit on the condition that Barclays Card Services or any representative admits that they obtained my information from a consumer reporting agency and will not issue myself the credit for a reason outside of adverse action. The response letter must be signed under penalty of perjury and must be notarized. Also, admit to being in violation of 15 U.S. Code 1681q - Obtaining information under false pretenses : Any person who knowingly and willfully obtains information on a consumer from a consumer reporting agency under false pretenses shall be fined under title 18, imprisoned for not more than 2 years, or both, as well as 18 U.S. Code 1951 - Interference with commerce : Whoever in any way or degree obstructs, delays, or affects commerce by extortion or attempts or conspires so to do, to any person or property in furtherance of a plan or purpose to do anything in violation of this section shall be fined under this title or imprisoned not more than twenty years, or both.

So as you can see, some pretty hefty fines. Or Barclays Card Services can choose to act in my best interest and issue the credit card to me, as I definitely need this in order to buy cleaning supplies and vinyl flooring for my house as well as a camera to XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX 

I expect Barclays Card Services to address these concerns in compliance with the relevant legal standards and take immediate corrective actions where necessary. I look forward to your prompt and detailed response to this matter. You can reach me by phone to verify who I am at XXXX or by mail. 

**Application ID : XXXX Sincerely, XXXX XXXX

_source.complaint_what_happened:
I submitted an application to CAPITAL ONE on XX/XX/XXXX. On XX/XX/XXXX I received an Adverse Action Letter from them as well. The adverse action offer stated that the application was rejected. 

According to 12 CFR 360.6 ( 2 ) the credit application is a FINANCIAL ASSET as well as SELF-LIQUIDATING PAPER according to 17 CFR 260.11 b-6.

The ADVERSE ACTION is in violation of the following : 15 U.S.C 78j, 15 U.S.C. 78ff, 15 U.S.C 1602 ( I ), 15 U.S.C 1691 ( a ) ( 3 ), 18 U.S.C. 241, 18 U.S.C. 242. 

I sent a letter to address/express the crucial consumer rights and safeguards that are relevant to credit transactions. These are enshrined in Title 15 of the United States Code, the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ), the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), the Credit Card Act of 2009, the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act ( SCRA ), the Privacy Act of 1974, the Uniform Commerical Code ( UCC ), Law Merchant, Generally Accepted Accounting Principals ( GAAP ), among other pivotal laws, regulations, and case law. 

Non-Discrimination in Credit Granting : As per the Equal Credit Opportunity Act, Title 15, Section 1691, your institution is legally bound not to deny credit based on race, color, religion, national origin, sex, marital status, age, or source of income. This Act underscores the principle of equal access to credit for all consumers, thereby cultivating a fair and non-discriminatory financial marketplace.

Limitations on the Use of Credit Reports : As stipulated by the FCRA, Title 15, Sections 1681-1681x, only information from my credit application can be used to evaluate my creditworthiness. A violation occurs if my credit reports are used unjustly to deny credit, thereby ensuring a fair assessment of my ability to repay any credit extended. 

Use and Protection of Social Security Numbers : The Privacy Act of 1974, specifically Section 7 ( a ) ( 1 ), distinctly prohibits any federal, state, or local government agency from denying any right, benefit, or privilege provided by law because of an individuals refusal to disclose their Social Security Number. In conjunction with the Social Security Act, Section 208 ( 42 U.S.C 408 ) the provisions safeguard my Social Security Number ( SSN ) from misuse. Misuse of my SSN or refusal to extend credit due to my unwillingness to provide my SSN infringes upon these Acts, carrying grave repercussions, including criminal charges, fines, and imprisonment. 

Safeguards Under the Credit Card Act : This Act offers protection against arbitrary interest rate increases, bans exorbitant fees, and enforces clear due dates and times, thereby ensuring that I am fully informed about the terms and conditions of my credit card, facilitating effective financial management. 
Unauthorized Use of Credit Card : According to Title 15 U.S.C 1602 ( I ) the term credit card means any card, plate, coupon book, or other credit device existing for the purpose of obtaining money, property, labor, or services on credit. Any card pertains to a social security card. Which classifies a credit card application denial or adverse action as an unauthorized use of a credit card due to them using the social to obtain money, property, or labor. 

Penalties for Non-Compliance with Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ) and Title 15 : Non-adherence to TILA or Title 15 provisions can result in substantial penalties as defined in Title 15, Section 1640- Civil Liability. These penalties may include compensation for actual damages suffered by the consumer due to the violation, statutory damages of up to {$4000.00} in individual actions or a sum equal to the lesser of {>= $1,000,000} or 1 % of the creditors net worth in class actions, and the recovery of the actions cost and attorneys fees. 

In light of these protections, I respectfully request that CAPITAL ONE, CFO : XXXX XXXX XXXX to strictly adhere to these regulatory provisions, statutory requirements, and established case law proceedings during our financial engagements. These legal guidelines are designed to uphold the integrity of the consumer credit market and shield consumers like me from potentially harmful financial practices. 
In particular, the unjustifiable denial of credit infringes upon the Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( ECOA ), which outlaws credit discrimination. Furthermore, inappropriate use of personal information, such as Social Security Numbers, in credit decisions contravenes the Privacy Act of 1974 and the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ). Under the principles of Generally Accepted Accounting Principles ( GAAP ), the Law Merchant, and the Uniform Commercial Code ( UCC ), transparency and fairness are fundamental to all credit transactions. 

Thank you for your attention to this significant matter. I anticipate engaging in fair, transparent, and lawful credit transactions. 


AS A REMINDER : DENIAL OF CREDIT IS INTERFERENCE WITH COMMERCE AND USING A CREDIT REPORT TO DENY ME MY CREDITS IS INTERFERENCE IN COMMERCE!!!!!!

_source.complaint_what_happened:
On XX/XX/year>, I made XXXX online purchases back-to-back from a travel website. However, the website glitched and XXXX purchase was charged twice. After trying to access my credit card account through bankofamerica.XXXX, I couldn't proceed without answering multiple questions about whether the transactions were authorized. 

I answered truthfully -- XXXX purchase was not authorized by me, but the other XXXX were correct, plus no one had stolen or gained access to my card information, and I was in possession of the card as well. I also typed an explanation into an available field about how the merchant 's website glitched and I didn't agree to a double-charge on only XXXX of the transactions. 

Bank of America immediately cancelled my card without my consent. The question screen was deceptive as it did not say I would lose my existing card number by simply reporting an erroneous double-charge. When I quickly called customer service within the next minute, a representative advised that a card with a new number would be issued to me. I explained there was no fraud and wanted my old card number back because I don't have time to update numerous auto-pay accounts, merchants, or websites with completely new information. The representative told me it was impossible to restore my card number despite my prompt action and explanation, and refused to assist me further. The amount of time I've already spent on this matter has been significant, including hours of lost family and personal activities. 

Bank of America is refusing to remedy this unfair situation, and their customer service representative clearly lacked authority and/or a willingness to override what a computer system had done. But my card number can easily be changed back, and to my knowledge, there is no legal prohibition on doing so. Bank of America should not be able to cancel a credit card without permission and especially after a call was made to seek immediate corrective action.

_source.complaint_what_happened:
On XX/XX/year> I check my credit card statement via the mobile app and see a {$6200.00} charge that I did not make. The charge was from the previous day ( XX/XX/year> ) made at a company called XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. 
I immediately contact my credit card company, USAA, and report the issue. The card is canceled and a fraud investigation is initiated. I am told that my account will be credited the money while the investigation occurs and that the fraud department will be in touch if they need anymore information from me. At this point, I believe that USAA is trying to help me through this stressful time of victimization. 
Days pass and I don't hear anything from the fraud department. I trust that they have found this to indeed to a fraudulent charge. Meanwhile other fraudulent charges are being attempted and denied on my canceled card. Weeks pass and I begin to have confidence that this nightmare is over. 
Then roughly XXXX weeks later on XX/XX/year> the {$6200.00} charge reappears on my card. I call USAA to inquire about this and initially the customer services reps can not tell me why this charge is back as there has been no letter or report from the fraud department. Several days later I do receive a message from the fraud department simply saying that my fraud claim has been denied and that I am responsible for the {$6200.00}! 
They have given me no reasons for the outcome of their investigation and no other information for their findings. I can not even make contact with them. I have called and asked for an explanation on multiple occasions but will not be put through with anyone in the fraud department. I have asked the service reps what information they need to help them believe me and they have no answer for me. 
They do not seek the truth of the matter. They don't want it to be fraud. They only want to deny and delay and hope that I will go away. 
I have been a customer of USAA for XXXX  years and the one time that I need them to believe me that I have been a victim of credit card fraud, they have basically called me a liar. 
They have this whole facade of being an organization that helps military and veterans. Well, I am a veteran and they are being anything but helpful in this matter.

_source.complaint_what_happened:

I gave an extra payment to pay the balance from purchases and keep only the no-interest balance. The Bank applied these extra payments on XX/XX/XXXX to my interest-free " balance transfer '' balance, instead of to my " purchases '' balance which was already accruing interest. 

I called the company two times. 

The first time they said I had to pay my balance in full to avoid interest. 

Later I researched a bit and found out there is a law forcing them to allocate extra payments to higher interest debt first. 

I called again, and they said that when I gave the payment, the purchases balance was still under a 0 % APR, so both balances were equivalent regarding interest, and he said that purchases balance had a 'lower ID ' or something like that. 

However, that means there was no way for me to avoid that interest because any payments would have gone to the balance transfer balance anyway, which makes their process fundamentally flawed and designed to charge interest when two 0 % APR with different expiration dates co-exist in the same account.

In fact, they've been applying one year 's worth of minimum payments ( which are calculated based on the total statement balance ) to the " balance transfer '' balance, despite that balance expiring later than the purchases balance, and thus being less likely to cause interest charges.

_source.complaint_what_happened:
Dear CFPB Representative, I am writing to file a formal complaint against American Express regarding the improper handling of my credit card accounts ending in XXXX. Despite repeated attempts to resolve these issues directly with American Express, they remain unresolved, causing significant inconvenience and potential financial harm.

Summary of Issues : Denial of Negotiable Instruments : American Express has been denying my negotiable instruments sent via registered mail, despite these being backed by the full faith and credit of the United States, as per 31 CFR 328.5 and the Indenture Agreement.

The Indenture Agreement defines " Eligible Investments '' to include negotiable instruments, which are guaranteed by the United States and should be accepted as payments.

Improper Payment Demands : American Express has unlawfully demanded payment in Federal Reserve Notes ( debt notes ), contrary to the submitted application used to open the account. This application, containing my personal and private financial information, acts as a financial asset, promissory note, and security satisfying each monthly obligation, as stipulated by 12 CFR 360.6 and 17 CFR 260.11b-6.

Article 1, Section 10, Clause 1 of the United States Constitution mandates that only gold and silver can lawfully discharge a debt, rendering the demand for Federal Reserve Notes improper.

Unauthorized Use and Securities Fraud : My application and personal financial information have been converted into asset-backed securities and traded on the secondary market, contrary to American Express 's statements to the SEC in their 424B2 prospectus.

This action constitutes securities fraud, money laundering, and racketeering, as American Express had assured the SEC that they would not trade these securities.

Failure to Perform Fiduciary Duties : American Express has breached their fiduciary duty under U.C.C. 3-307 by not managing my account equitably and failing to accept my lawful payments.

The use of my financial assets without providing any tangible benefit to me is an unauthorized action.

Prospectus and Indenture Agreement Violations : The prospectus ( Form 424B2 ) and Indenture Agreement stipulate that the securities related to my account would not be listed on any securities exchange or automated quotation system. However, this commitment has been violated, evidencing deceitful practices.

Credit Report Impact : American Express has not updated my credit report for the payment received in May, which could potentially harm my credit standing. Despite tendering payment on time each month, they have failed to reflect this accurately.

They credited my account for the full amount and then reversed it, but have yet to return any of my instruments.

I have appreciated the services provided by American Express and have sought to resolve this matter amicably and equitably. However, their ongoing failures compel me to seek your intervention to address these violations and ensure compliance with applicable laws and fiduciary duties.

_source.complaint_what_happened:
I am writing to file a formal complaint against Citibank for what I believe to be discriminatory practices that have affected not only myself but potentially countless other consumers in my industry. My concerns are rooted in both the unjust closure of my credit card accounts and the broader context of similar actions reportedly taken by Citibank against other individuals under questionable circumstances. 

As a longstanding Citibank customer of over 10 years, I have always maintained my accounts in excellent standing. Despite this, Citibank abruptly closed all of my credit card accounts without prior notification or a clear explanation. The only conceivable reason for this action appears to be my investment within the legal and state-regulated cannabis industry. This rationale for closing my accounts is not only discriminatory but also a punitive measure against my lawful employment. Over 100 people I have spoke to in IL have had their accounts suddenly closed with no explanation. No other financial institution has done this. 

Furthermore, there is reason to suspect that these closures may also be influenced by discriminatory practices potentially based on personal data, including my name or other identifiers, given Citibanks history and ongoing lawsuits alleging similar behavior. Such actions suggest a pattern of behavior where Citibank may be systematically targeting individuals based on their association with the cannabis industry or other discriminatory criteria. 

Context of Wider Issues : Citibank is currently facing multiple lawsuits alleging discriminatory practices. These lawsuits suggest a troubling pattern that aligns with my experience, indicating that my case is not isolated but part of a broader, systemic issue within the banks operations. This raises significant concerns about Citibank 's compliance with federal regulations designed to protect consumers from such discrimination. 

Impact and Request for Action : The closure of my accounts has not only caused significant personal inconvenience and financial disruption but also the forfeiture of accumulated rewards without recourse. This action has implications for my financial stability and credit rating, adding to the urgency of this complaint. 

Given the severity of these allegations and the potential violation of consumer rights, I urge the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau to : Conduct a thorough investigation into Citibanks practices regarding account closures. 
Assess the legality of Citibanks actions in the context of federal anti-discrimination laws. 

Take appropriate actions to ensure that affected consumers, including myself, are afforded justice and that such discriminatory practices are halted. 

I am prepared to provide any further information needed for this investigation and eagerly await your response on how this serious matter will be addressed. 

Thank you for your attention to this critical issue. I look forward to your prompt and decisive action.

These are enshrined in Title 15 of the United States Code, the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ), the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), the Credit Card Act of 2009, the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act ( SCRA ), the Privacy Act of 1974, the Uniform Commerical Code ( UCC ), Law Merchant, Generally Accepted Accounting Principals ( GAAP ), among other pivotal laws, regulations, and case law.

Non-Discrimination in Credit Granting : As per the Equal Credit Opportunity Act, Title 15, Section 1691, your institution is legally bound not to deny credit based on race, color, religion, national origin, sex, maritial status, age, or source of income. This Act underscores the principle of equal access to credit for all consumers, thereby cultivating a fair and non-discriminatory financial marketplace.

Limitations on the Use of Credit Reports : As stipulated by the FCRA, Title 15, Sections 1681-1681x, only information from my credit application can be used to evaluate my creditworthiness. A violation occurs if my credit reports are used unjustly to deny credit, thereby ensuring a fair assessment of my ability to repay any credit extended. 

Use and Protection of Social Security Numbers : The Privacy Act of 1974, specifically Section 7 ( a ) ( 1 ), distinctly prohibits any federal, state, or local government agency from denying any right, benefit, or privilege provided by law because of an individuals refusal to disclose their Social Security Number. In conjunction with the Social Security Act, Section 208 ( 42 U.S.C 408 ) the provisions safeguard my Social Security Number ( SSN ) from misuse. Misuse of my SSN or refusal to extend credit due to my unwillingness to provide my SSN infringes upon these Acts, carrying grave repercussions, including criminal charges, fines, and imprisonment.

Safeguards Under the Credit Card Act : This Act offers protection against arbitrary interest rate increases, bans exorbitant fees, and enforces clear due dates and times, thereby ensuring that I am fully informed about the terms and conditions of my credit card, facilitating effective financial management.

Unauthorized Use of Credit Card : According to Title 15 U.S.C 1602 ( I ) the term credit card means any card, plate, coupon book, or other credit device existing for the purpose of obtaining money, property, labor, or services on credit. Any card pertains to a social security card. Which classifies a credit card application denial or adverse action as an unauthorized use of a credit card due to them using the social to obtain money, property, or labor.

Penalties for Non-Compliance with Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ) and Title 15 : Non-adherence to TILA or Title 15 provisions can result in substantial penalties as defined in Title 15, Section 1640- Civil Liability. These penalties may include compensation for actual damages suffered by the consumer due to the violation, statutory damages of up to {$4000.00} in individual actions or a sum equal to the lesser of {>= $1,000,000} or 1 % of the creditors net worth in class actions, and the recovery of the actions cost and attorneys fees.

In light of these protections, I respectfully request that XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX to strictly adhere to these regulatory provisions, statutory requirements, and established case law proceedings during our financial engagements. These legal guidelines are designed to uphold the integrity of the consumer credit market and shield consumers like me from potentially harmful financial practices. 
In particular, the unjustifiable denial of credit infringes upon the Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( ECOA ), which outlaws credit discrimination. Furthermore, inappropriate use of personal information, such as Social Security Numbers, in credit decisions contravenes the Privacy Act of 1974 and the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ). Under the principles of Generally Accepted Accounting Principles ( GAAP ), the Law Merchant, and the Uniform Commercial Code ( UCC ), transparency and fairness are fundamental to all credit transactions. 

Thank you for your attention to this significant matter. I anticipate engaging in fair, transparent, and lawful credit transactions.

_source.complaint_what_happened:
Due to issues Ill explain, they have made it next to impossible to find exact dates on everything. 

In XXXX, I opened an account with PayPal Credit ( formerly XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX ). Of course, being a XXXX college student at the time I ran the bill up and began to struggle to make the payments each month but I did manage to make them until XX/XX/XXXX when, according to my credit report, I became 30 days late ( the reason I say according to my credit report is that I am unable to go back before XXXX in my bank history and, for a bit, was forced to pay via XXXX XXXX. So I am unsure if that is entirely accurate ). 

Around the same time, PayPal Credit was purchased by Synchrony Bank which at least in my perspective did not go smoothly. The PayPal credit tab would frequently not appear on the site and, when it actually did, it would experience downtime that would last between 48 hours to, at one point, 2 weeks. During the two weeks period they reminded people the day before that the site would be down and that if you had a payment due during that period you should make the payment prior to the downtime which was absolutely impossible for me with the payment schedule I had. 

Prior to the switch to Synchrony, I had called ( they wouldnt let me do it through the site or email ) requesting my address change from Florida back to MA. During this switch, it either seemed to revert or just be ignored, because I never received any physical mail stating that my account was to be closed or charged off. My guess is that it was all sent to my former Florida address. I learned of my account closure by logging onto the site and being unable to XXXX tab ( I initially assumed it was just downtime, but after a month realized it was probably gone ). I assume it closed in XXXX XXXX or XX/XX/XXXX. So I began paying what I could every month via my banks XXXX XXXX. This went on for a few months until I received a request via email to stop submitting via XXXX XXXX as it was with a debt collector. I was baffled, as I had not been informed, and I learned that it had been officially charged off by a steep incline in my credit score and a little C/O symbol on the account. 

I called as soon as I found out. I asked if I could pay the debt and they said no, I would have to pay the debt collector. When I inquired what agency it was with, they initially wouldnt tell me. I finally got someone who said that it was likely with a certain company because that was like one or two of the ones they sold to. So I sent an email to the debt collection agency and they happily confirmed that it was them who the debt was with and requested that I call. So I did. I told them about the situation I had been through and they were sympathetic, and I scheduled a date to pay. I officially paid off the entire amount about a month or two later. 

Here is why I am submitting to the CFPB : While it is my fault that the debt became late and that I was struggling financially. I do believe that I was stuck in a wrong place at the wrong time scenario. I believe that I shouldnt have to suffer due to a messy takeover of a company. The amount of opportunities that I have lost credit wise over the years due to this is insane and its kept my credit score extremely low. It also made it so Synchrony really wont consider me for anything Ive tried writing to the Synchrony & PayPal regarding this and theyve said multiple times that they wont do anything about it ( I also reached out to the Debt Collector, who essentially told me to talk to Synchrony, but then informed me that paying it would essentially remove the charge off from my account and that obviously didnt happen ).

_source.complaint_what_happened:
I have an XXXX XXXX XXXX credit card with Chase. This card provides a feature called EPP ( Equal Pay Promo ) whereby when I buy items on XXXX over a minimum amount, there is an option to pay over an extended time ( XXXX  months, XXXX  months, XXXX  months ) at XXXX  % APR. 
I had taken a balance transfer offer from the card at XXXX  % XXXX until XX/XX/XXXX for which I am making the minimum payments every month. I was made to understand that if I made any new purchases after a balance transfer, those purchases would start accruing interest right away. So, I paid off all my new purchase balance to make sure no interest would be charged. I confirmed with Customer Care and paid a last amount of {$10.00} on XX/XX/XXXX whereby they confirmed after that no new purchase interest would be charged unless I made more new purchases. Further, I was told that there would be no interest charged if I made Equal Pay Promo purchases and paid the EPP monthly amounts in full till the promo lasted ( XX/XX/XXXX months ). I asked customer service multiple times to confirm that Equal Pay Promo purchases will not accrue any interest even when I had a balance transfer promo going on. After these multiple confirmations, I made sure that I only made EPP purchases on XXXX. No other new purchase outside of EPP has been made since then.

But I started seeing that I was being charged interest under the Purchases category every month. I called customer care and asked them which purchases were accruing interest since I had not made any purchases outside of EPP and EPP does not accrue interest. At this they could not give me any details of the purchases that were accruing interest, but the rep waived the small interest of ~ {$2.00} at that point.

But next month, again I saw interest charges coming back under purchase category even when I had made no purchase outside of EPP. So, I wrote a secure message to Chase on May 13the, 2024, asking for clarification. There were a few messages back and forth, but they failed to clarify the issue. They kept beating around the bush about balance transfers and new purchases but did not answer the actual question about how I was being charged interest on EPPs when EPPs dont accrue interest if paid off during the promo period.

Then I called customer service and talked to a supervisor this time. He kept me on hold for a long time and then came back and said he saw some purchases on his end that were not showing EPP even though on my side, every purchase shows as an EPP purchase on the credit card statement, and hence the interest was being charged. He said he would escalate this issue and the bank will send me a mail stating what they found.

Chase sent me a mail dated XX/XX/XXXX. In this letter they said that unfortunately they can not reverse the charge because they have determined the amount of interest is correct. They again did not give me any details of which purchases were accruing interest. 
I am extremely unhappy with this experience. Chase customer care is not giving the right information repeatedly and they are being completely non-transparent about the interest charges. I have had a similar bad experience with them late last year about a balance transfer and wrong information being provided to me multiple times, which I brought up with CFPB ( Complaint ID XXXX ) and Chase then got back to me and resolved the issue. But this seems to be a perpetual problem with them where they dont provide the right information, are not transparent, and are wrongly charging me interest. 

I would request CFPB to please look into this matter and help me get this resolved.

The caller said that the compromised card would be cancelled ( I later found out from the Elan fraud group that it was not ), and a new card would be sent to us. We said that we were travelling and would be in XXXX for several weeks. We provided a XXXX address to which the new cards should be sent. Shortly after that call ended I got an email from Fidelity Card Services ( I confirmed that it was issued by Elan ) indicating that new cards would be sent to us. The woman representative let me know she " could submit a request, but since the card has not been opened for 6 months the result of the increase request will not be in my favor ''. _source.complaint_what_happened:
On XX/XX/XXXX, I made a reservation via the Capital One Travel portal for the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ( confirmation XXXX ) for check in on XX/XX/XXXX and check-out on XX/XX/XXXX. This reservation was for two Double Rooms ( non-smoking ) and booked using the Capital One Venture X. 

On XX/XX/XXXX at XXXX XXXX  ( local time ), I checked into the hotel but was told by the front desk staff that the reservation was for two smoking rooms and that we would be assigned to two smoking rooms. I pushed back, noting that I had reserved a non-smoking Double Room and requested this. The hotel said they could give me one non-smoking room, but there was no availability for a Smoking room. The front desk staff also showed me my reservation on their system, noting that a Smoking room was reserved. They were unreceptive to my concerns that I had originally booked a non-smoking room on the Capital One Travel portal, and they declined requests for compensation and room changes. They also noted that I could choose to cancel the smoking room, but would still be responsible for the cost of the room as the reservation was non-refundable. 

I called Capital One XXXX at XXXX XXXX  to discuss the situation, first seeking verification that I had, in fact, reserved a non-smoking room. The agent and I agreed that this is what I reserved. The two options for reservations for Double Rooms include Double Room and Double Room, Smoking Allowed. ( see attached screenshots ). The agent noted that the original reservation was, in fact, for a non-smoking room, and we are confused as to why the hotel is not honoring this request. This is of particular importance to me as a member of my traveling party is allergic to smoke and living in a smoking room would pose a significant health hazard. 

I requested a refund and compensation from the agent but she said that Capital One can only provide a refund if the hotel agrees to it. Since the hotel staff refuses to even acknowledge the original non-smoking reservation, they will not provide the requested refund. This is disappointing, as I explicitly booked two non-smoking rooms and my request was not honored and I am not receiving any compensation to cancel my booking and stay at a new hotel.

_source.complaint_what_happened:
To whom it may concern : This letter will serve as an explanation of the events in regard to the charge of {$390.00} made by the fraudulent company XXXX XXXX, on my Capital One XXXX card. 

I had been contacted several times over text messages by XXXX ( see uploaded texts ) starting in XXXX of this year. After several attempts, I agreed to speak with their representative who told me his name is XXXX XXXX. I have no idea if it actually is his name, but I suspect it is a fake name. He informed me that if I signed up for their program, I would receive several qualified real estate leads per week. Further he stated that the leads would begin arriving the week that I signed up. I had some hesitation about moving forward, but he was able to convince me that his company was a legitimate company. He also told me that he would be my point of contact moving forward, and that if I had any issues to reach out to him. I decided to move forward, and part of the reason was knowing that if I used my Capital One XXXX, I would be able to dispute the charge if the transaction turned out to be fraudulent. After the charge was made, I never heard from XXXX XXXX or XXXX again. No leads were delivered, as were promised and paid for. 

After about 9 days of waiting for the leads to be assigned over to me, I reached out to XXXX via text message ( again see text docs ), which he said was the best way to contact him. I asked when I could expect to received the leads as promised. He did not respond. I got very busy with work, and then reached out to him about 18 days after my first text message, as I still had not received any of the promised leads, and again here was no response. 

I knew that this was a fraudulent company, but the lack of response confirmed it for me. I decided to dispute the charge. After the dispute, XXXX was contacted by either Capital One or XXXX, and produced a document with my electronic signature as proof of the charge. Whether or not I authorized the initial charge is not in dispute. However, the point of the dispute is that XXXX never provided the service that was paid for. Even since the initial charge was made over 3 months ago, I have not received any real estate leads from XXXX, and have not been contacted by XXXX XXXX, or anyone else from XXXX. If this was a legitimate company, would they not have reached out after the dispute was filed, to try and rectify and resolve the situation? 

Instead, they are relying on the electronic signature on a document offering fraudulent services, to try and steal the {$390.00} from me. The simple point is that if they had provided what they originally offered, I would have no issues with paying them for what we agreed upon. If you look at the history of this card, there is not a history of disputes. As we are happy to pay for goods and services at an agreed upon price. XXXX XXXX is that XXXX has not provided anything that they have offered. Once I did some digging online into these companies, I quickly discovered that many other people have had the same issues. Also, since this has happened, I have been contacted by several other companies all offering the same services. To test them, I tell them that I will not sign up for any service that requires an up front fee. They all have the same spiel that XXXX had, that this is needed to secure my willingness to work with them. Once I tell them firmly that I will not be paying an up front fee, predictably, they cease to contact me. 

This is the heart of the scam. Get people to pay an up front fee, if they dispute the charge pull out the agreement, and hope the victim get dejected and just drops the issue. 

I will not be dropping this issue. 

If Capital One/XXXX XXXXllows criminals to use their platforms for this type of illicit fraudulent behavior, then that is not only allowing fraud against their customer, but even worse, is actually aiding and abetting this fraud. Not only should I receive my refund, but XXXX should stop allowing XXXX Solutions to use their platform to facilitate scamming money from any more people, who are just trying to make a legitimate living. 

If my dispute is declined, I will have to move forward with filing a complaint with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, as well as reaching out to my local representatives for the federal government, to try and hold financial institutions accountable for the types of entities they do business with. 

If you have any questions or concerns about this matter, please feel free to reach out to me directly. 

Thank you for your time. 


XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX

_source.complaint_what_happened:
I have a credit card with Wells Fargo that is just for day to day spending. I have had the card since XXXX and pay a set amount with every bi-weekly paycheck so that the previous statement balance is satisfied and I do not have to pay any interest. 

For the XX/XX/XXXX statement, I was responsible for a balance of {$410.00}, due by XX/XX/XXXX. I paid {$400.00} ( + {$13.00} via rewards credit ) before XX/XX/XXXX, and another scheduled payment of {$200.00} was transferred on XX/XX/XXXX. I was unaware that the balance of {$5.00} was late by 2 days, but I was appalled to see that i had been charged interest in the amount of {$5.00}. The interest charge was more than the remaining balance on the account, so I called to complain. 

The Wells Fargo representative offered to dispute the interest charge, but told me that the policy is not to charge interest based on the previous balance or any payments during that month, but instead to charge interest based on the current balance including all new charges. To make sure I understood, I asked whether that interest calculation would therefore include a large hypothetical purchase on the day just before a payment was due. The representative confirmed that even new transactions that were only a day old would be included in the calculation of interest charges, even though they were not within the time frame where interest should be accruing. 

I would be surprised if this was a legal practice, even if the language is somewhere in the customer agreement. I am able to dispute and/or pay my modest penalty, but other people must have much harder times making any progress if they suffer from these dishonest practices. I hope that by sharing this information, progress can be made to help protect people from this type of predatory lending.

I told XXXX that I was not going back to the area of the reservation, that I expected a full refund ( not being charged any amount given the circumstances ). The next day, I also provided proof to XXXX that the host messaged me details which indicated that the listing was inaccurate. XXXX took three days to refund me, and they kept 3 nights of my original reservation payment, despite that I never officially checked in and spent those 3 nights in my vehicle. I was charged for services that I did not receive. I filed a dispute with Citi on XXXX XXXX given how XXXX was sluggish to simply refund me. After initiating this dispute, I spent almost XXXX hours across 5 months fighting for the refund I was rightfully owed. I provided them various proof of all that happened -- messages from the merchant 's platform, proof that the listing was inaccurate, and phone call logs of all of my attempts to resolve the situation. Citi was quick on several occasions to send me a " canned '' response, and there were absolute indications that Citi did not exercise due diligence to protect me as a consumer, for a situation where my life was endangered. During one of my last attempts to address the dispute with Citi, a manager in the credit card department had the gall to debate with me about my dispute. I am certain that if the appropriate governing entity were to audit the investigation Citi performed, they would find obvious evidence that Citi failed to follow protocols to protect me under credit laws. This credit card has been open for at least 8 years, and I have spent hundreds of thousands on this card as my primary method of payment. I would close the credit card, but that would have a negative impact on my credit score. I will barely use this credit card going forward, since I can not rely on Citi to follow basic protocols that other credit card issuers follow to protect consumers. I already closed my Citi savings account.

_source.complaint_what_happened:
I am writing to formally lodge a complaint against PNC Bank regarding deceptive credit card terms and unfair treatment. My issue concerns a credit card that I received from PNC Bank, which was advertised and documented in the accompanying terms as having a 0 % interest rate for the first 9 months. Unfortunately, this promise was not honored, resulting in significant financial and reputational harm to me. 

Here are the details of my complaint : Misleading Terms : Upon receipt of the PNC credit card, the terms enclosed in the envelope explicitly stated that the card would carry a 0 % interest rate for the first 9 months. 
Based on this information, I made a purchase of {$20000.00} with the expectation that I would have 9 months to pay off the balance without incurring any interest. 

Unexpected Interest Charges : When I received my first bill, I was shocked to find that I had been charged an interest rate of over 17 % on my {$20000.00} purchase. 
I promptly contacted PNC Bank to rectify this issue, explaining that the terms provided with the card clearly indicated a 0 % introductory interest rate. 

Inadequate Response and Prolonged Resolution : During my initial call with PNC Bank, I was informed that there was no 0 % introductory period for my card, contrary to the documented terms I had received. 
On XX/XX/year> I subsequently sent PNC Bank a copy of the terms that were included with the credit card, which clearly outlined the 0 % interest for the first 9 months. 
Despite my efforts, PNC Bank has been unresponsive and has failed to provide a timely resolution. It has been almost a month since I provided the documentation, and I am repeatedly told that " these things take time '' without any further action or proposed resolution. 

Negative Impact on Credit Profile and Banking Relationship : In the interim, PNC Bank has revoked my credit card and reported adverse information to my credit profile, which has negatively impacted my credit score.

This action is particularly distressing as I have multiple accounts with PNC Bank, including personal and business accounts, and two other credit cards that are all in good standing and paid on time.

I have expressed my willingness to pay off the card immediately and close the account if the 0 % interest rate for 9 months can not be honored. However, I have yet to receive any communication or resolution from PNC Bank. 
The deceptive advertising, failure to honor documented terms, and subsequent mishandling of my complaint by PNC Bank have caused undue stress and financial harm. I believe this matter warrants immediate investigation and resolution by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau. 

I request that the CFPB intervene to ensure that PNC Bank : Honors the 0 % interest rate for the first 9 months as originally documented.

Corrects any negative information reported to my credit profile as a result of this issue. 
Provides a timely and satisfactory resolution to this complaint. 

Thank you for your attention to this matter. Please do not hesitate to contact me if you require any additional information or documentation. 

I look forward to your assistance in resolving this issue promptly.

Subject : Notice of Violations under UCC and Administrative Procedures Act Sales & Client Service Specialist at Truist Dept. 
TRUIST XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. 
XXXX, North Carolina XXXX Dear XXXX XXXX, I am writing to formally bring to your attention an issue regarding the recent reduction of my credit card limit for my account ending in XXXX. I received a letter dated XX/XX/year> from TRUIST informing me that TRUIST periodically conducts a review of the original creditors [ Myself, XXXX XXXX, a natural living person ] account [ without 45 days prior notice which is required according to the Administrative Procedures Act ]. TRUIST decided that they were going to reduce my credit card and they did this without even giving me the option to appeal the decision. My credit limit has been reduced from {$13000.00} to {$9000.00}. This action was taken without prior notice or a valid reason and thereby adversely affecting my credit profile [ No 3rd party credit reporting agency has anything from me with my wet ink signature verifying any of the info that is being reported, which is required by law before adding it to my credit profile to ensure accuracy ] and financial planning which resulted in several violations. It is stated in your correspondence that this decision may have been influenced by information on my credit report, which I have not verified. Additionally, I was not given prior notice regarding this action. Both of these actions are violations of the Uniform Commercial Code ( UCC ) and the Administrative Procedures Act.

Violation # 1 : As per UCC 1-304, every contract or duty within the UCC imposes an obligation of good faith in its performance and enforcement. The sudden and unjustified reduction of my credit limit without adequate notice or explanation is a breach of this obligation. 
The UCC 's requirement for good faith, defined in UCC 1-201 ( b ) ( 20 ) as " honesty in fact and the observance of reasonable commercial standards of fair dealing, '' was not observed in this instance. 

The reason given by TRUIST in the letter was that TRUIST used a scoring model provided by XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX a privately owned company that DOES NOT have anything in writing from myself [ a natural living person ] giving my consent or permission with my wet ink signature on it, nor have I given TRUIST or XXXX my consent to share any information about my private contracts and agreements that have in fact negatively impacted me due to this unwarranted action. 

Violation # 2 : 18 USC 894 TRUIST and XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX are teaming up to conspire ( anyone who in secret, joins or teams up with another to jointly commit an unlawful act ) against me. 

TRUIST can not use any information that has never been verified by me and without my permission or without giving prior notice, to make decisions about my account. The account is with TRUIST. TRUIST DOES NOT own the account. 

Violation # 3 : This action is in violation of the Uniform Commercial Code ( UCC ), specifically in relation to adverse action notices. 

According to UCC Article 9, Part 6 ( Section 9-614 ), regarding the right of a debtor to receive timely notification of adverse action affecting their credit arrangements, TRUIST is required to provide proper notice of any adverse action taken on my account, including but not limited to the reduction of my credit card limit. 

The reduction of my credit card limit without appropriate and timely notification constitutes a violation of the aforementioned UCC provision. 


Ensure that any future adverse actions comply fully with UCC requirements, including providing adequate notice as stipulated in Section 9-614. 
Failure to comply with these requests will result in further action to protect my rights under the UCC. 

According to UCC Article 9, Part 6 ( Section 9-614 ), regarding the right of a debtor to receive timely notification of adverse action affecting their credit arrangements, TRUIST is required to provide proper notice of any adverse action taken on my account, including but not limited to the reduction of my credit card limit. 

The reduction of my credit card limit without appropriate and timely notification constitutes a violation of the aforementioned UCC provision. I request that Truist Bank : Ensure that any future adverse actions comply fully with UCC requirements, including providing adequate notice as stipulated in Section 9-614. 
Failure to comply with these requests will result in further action to protect my rights under the UCC. 

Violation # 4 : UCC 1-202. Notice ; Knowledge. According to UCC 1-202, proper notice must be given to the party concerned regarding any changes or decisions that may affect them. In this case, no such notice was given to me prior to the reduction of my credit limit. 

Violation # 5 : UCC 2-609. Right to Adequate Assurance of Performance. Under UCC 2-609, a party to a contract has the right to request assurance from the other party if they have reasonable grounds for insecurity. TRUIST unilateral decision to reduce my credit limit without verification or prior notice undermines this right. 

Violation # 6 : 5 U.S.C. 552. Public Information ; Agency Rules, Opinions, Orders, Records, and Proceedings. According to 5 U.S.C. 552, agencies must follow due process in their decision-making procedures. By failing to provide prior notice or the opportunity to verify the information on my credit report, Truist Bank has not adhered to the required administrative processes. 

Violation # 7 : 5 U.S.C. 706. Scope of Review. This section outlines the judicial review of agency actions, ensuring that all procedures are followed properly and rights are not infringed. TRUISTs actions are subject to review under this provision for failure to provide notice and verification, thereby violating the prescribed administrative procedures. 

Violation # 8 : UCC 1-304. Obligation of Good Faith. Under UCC 1-304, every contract or duty within the UCC imposes an obligation of good faith in its performance and enforcement. TRUIST 's actions, including the failure to verify the information on my credit report and the lack of prior notice, violate this obligation of good faith. 


Violation # 9 : 15 U.S. Code 1637 ( i ) requires creditors to provide a 45-day advance notice before increasing the APR or making other significant changes to the terms of a credit card account. This allows consumers time to opt-out of the changes if they choose. 

Violation # 10 : 15 U.S. Code subsection 1691 which is the Scope of Prohibition. That section defines the term adverse action as a denial or revocation of credit, a change in the terms of an existing credit arrangement, or a refusal to grant credit in substantially the amount or on substantially the terms requested.

_source.complaint_what_happened:
This call took place XX/XX/XXXX at XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and lasted 36 minutes. The call was made to American Express at XXXX. 
Called American Express to update the company with tracking information about a Claim Notice, as instructed in the Platinum Card from American Express XXXX XXXX - XXXX Resolution - Sending a Claim Notice, I sent to American Express XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX  XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX  XXXX New York XXXX XXXX regarding one lost payment I sent in via Certified Mail tracking on XX/XX/XXXX and one payment, again via Certified Mail tracking, I sent XX/XX/XXXX American Express refused to process after accepting. Neither were returned to me to this day despite my request. 
The automated system took me to an agent that I began speaking with to let him know I was following up on a call I made Wednesday, XX/XX/XXXX as I was receiving calls from American Express notifying me the company would be canceling my account due to non-payment. 
I informed the agent I spoke with that I am following up to inform them not to take any adverse action on my account because I submitted a Claim Notice on XX/XX/XXXX and have not yet heard anything back from American Express XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX and we are actively in the 30 day process. 
The agent began asking me questions about my account, my payment, when I sent in the payment, the type of payment and other information about my previous attempts to make a payment on my card. 
I informed the agent that I sent in a negotiable instrument and the agent informed me he didn't know what that was and if I could explain to him 'for his own education '. I informed the agent that extensive details were in my Claim Notice and other correspondence I sent to the company, the company 's CFO, XXXX XXXX XXXX ( which forwarded my emails to his assistant, XXXX ), the trustee and its SEC listed agents XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX, and XXXX XXXX, the paying agent, the transferor, American Express Legal, American Express Office of Executive Escalations, RFC, TRS, among other, about my repeated attempts to make payments and correspondence recently sent to American Express XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX 
The agent asked me to hold and came back to tell me that he was instructed to share a new American Express Policy that states negotiable instruments are not valid forms of payment and that he would be happy to tell me what an acceptable payment actually is and insisted on convincing me negotiable instruments are not acceptable forms of payments. 
This is deeply concerning and confusing to me because the XXXX XXXX from American Express Cardmember Agreement, in which I entered when I started my contract with American Express, clearly states on page 3 of Section 2, How to make a payment bullet point two : " a single negotiable instrument clearable through the U.S. banking system ''. 
Again, deeply concerning and confusing to me from a financial institution as massive as American Express Company, specifically given my journey of trying to make a payment to my account and the late fees, negative credit reporting, and recent threat to cancel my account, is clearly misleading and deceptive, unsafe and unsound practice in direct contradiction to the Certain Legal Aspects of the Receivables, Certain Regulatory Matters and Consumer Financial Products Regulation of the American Express Prospectus dated XX/XX/XXXX which clearly states : " The operations and financial condition of XXXX are subject to extensive regulation and supervision under federal and state law. The appropriate banking regulatory authorities, including the FDIC, the OCC and the CFPB have broad enforcement powers over XXXX. These enforcement powers may adversely affect the operation and financial condition of the trust and your rights under the pooling and servicing agreement prior to the appointment of a receiver or conservator. 
If United States federal bank regulatory authorities supervising the bank were to find that any obligation of the bank or an affiliate under a securitization or other agreement, or any activity of the bank or such affiliate, constituted an unsafe or unsound practice or violated any law, rule, regulation or written condition or agreement applicable to the bank or such affiliate, such federal bank regulatory authorities have the power to order the bank or such affiliate, among other things, to rescind such agreement or contract, refuse to perform that obligation, terminate the activity, amend the terms of such obligation or take such other action as such regulatory authorities determine to be appropriate. '' and Certain Legal Aspects of the Receivables, Consumer Financial Products Regulation : " The relationship of the consumer and the provider of consumer credit is extensively regulated by federal and state consumer protection laws. With respect to credit accounts issued by XXXX, the most significant federal laws include the federal Truth in Lending, Equal Credit Opportunity, Fair Credit Reporting and Fair Debt Collection Practices Acts. These statutes impose disclosure requirements before and when an account is opened, at the end of monthly billing cycles and on an annual basis, and, in addition, limit account holder liability for unauthorized use, prohibit certain discriminatory practices in extending credit, and regulate practices followed in collections. In addition, account holders are entitled under these laws to have payments and credits applied to the revolving credit account promptly and to request prompt resolution of billing errors. 
The CFPB has broad rulemaking examination and enforcement authority with respect to certain federal consumer financial laws over providers of consumer financial products and services, including American Express and XXXX, and authority to prevent unfair, deceptive or abusive acts or practices. '' An agent from American Express Company reading off a new American Express policy stating a direct contradiction of the Cardmember Agreement 's accepted methods of payment is unfair, deceptive and abusive, unsafe and unsound, is the employment of a deceptive and manipulated device, and raises the question if new accounts are being opened today with the promise of negotiable instruments being an accepted form of payment when, in fact, American Express and its affiliates has NO intention of honoring that clause of the binding contract. 
The agent informed me the call was being recorded by American Express, the confirmation number the agent gave me for this call is GC - XXXX and the Complaint number generated as a result of this call is XXXX.

_source.complaint_what_happened: On XX/XX/XXXX, my parents received a Capital One credit card in the mail to their home address in Nebraska that was opened in my name, so they notified me via text the same day about the credit card to see if I opened a new account. I have lived in North Carolina since XX/XX/XXXX. I did not open the account, so I called Capital One right away on XX/XX/XXXX at XXXX ( XXXX  ) & the call lasted XXXX minutes. I was connected to a Capital One agent who I explained to that I was a victim of identity theft and that I did not open this credit card account. At the time of the call, the account 's balance was {$0.00} and I asked the agent to close the credit card completely so no one could access it or use it and to put a fraud alert on my account. When getting my personal info, the agent revealed that a different address & phone number were used to open the account, but the agent would not give me that information. I gave the agent my personal information in order to be contacted about the investigation. The agent confirmed that he put the fraud alert on my personal information with Capital One and that he closed the account & told me I would receive a letter in the mail after Capital One investigated the account letting me know their findings. I never received that letter. My parents shredded the Capital One credit card. I put a fraud alert on my credit through XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX. On XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX ( which I subscribe to ) alerted me that I had exceeded my credit limit. I called XXXX first who instructed me to call Capital One again. XXXX informed me that someone had spent {$10000.00} on the Capital One credit card ( limit was {$10000.00} ) that I had not opened. I did not make these transactions. XXXX also informed me that the Capital One account was opened on XX/XX/XXXX. I called Capital One again on XX/XX/XXXX at XXXX ( XXXX  ). I explained what happened to the agent and asked how it was possible that the credit card was used after I closed the account & she said the fraud alert was on the account but that the account was never closed. She wouldn't provide me with any information from my first phone call with Capital One. I told her to close the account again and she said that she closed it & refused to send me an email confirmation but gave me a case number. She said they would investigate and send me a letter. I then received a letter from Capital One in the mail that was dated XX/XX/XXXX saying that Capital One found me to be responsible for the account claiming that I opened the account and had activity with the account, meaning they spent no more than 1 day investigating my claims. The letter says nothing about the fraud alert or identity theft. XXXX suggested that I file a police report and FTC report and call Capital One again to reinstate the claim. I filed the police report on XX/XX/XXXX and the FTC report on XX/XX/XXXX. I also froze my credit reports with XXXX, XXXX, and XXXX as advised by XXXX. I then called Capital One on XX/XX/XXXX to reinstate my fraud claim and gave them the police report information. The agent would not take the FTC report number to add to the case. When confirming my contact information, the agent said they have a different email and phone number on file but that she could not share that information with me. I was connected to a different agent to update my phone number and email address for them to contact me. I have received no calls or emails from Capital One. I have only received the letters in the mail mentioned in this complaint as the only form of contact with Capital One. I then received a letter in the mail from Capital One dated XX/XX/XXXX ( the same day I called ) stating the exact same findings as the first letter : that I was responsible for the account. Capital One took less than XXXX hours to investigate my claim even after providing them with a police report. My agent with XXXX then joined me on the next call to Capital One on XX/XX/XXXX to reinstate the claim again. We made sure the agent put the police report number, the FTC report number, and my correct contact information in the complaint. Additionally, we asked the agent to make sure that Capital One actually made an effort this time to investigate the claim since the previous investigations took 1 day or less, which the XXXX XXXX put in the complaint notes. Again, I received no calls or emails from Capital One. I then received a letter from Capital One dated XX/XX/XXXX stating the same thing as the previous letters : that Capital One found me responsible for the account due to activity on the account indicating that I opened and interacted with the account. I have no access to the Capital One account at all and I did not open the account. Additionally, the charges listed on that letter now amount to {$10000.00}. After receiving this letter, XXXX advised that I file a complaint with the CFPB. My credit score has decreased substantially and I now have to file disputes with all reporting agencies in order to try to resolve this since Capital One refuses to investigate my identity theft claim. I have proof of address in North Carolina since XX/XX/XXXX.

_source.complaint_what_happened:
On or about XX/XX/year> I was using my card to make purchases related to a recent move. Synchrony Bank, flagged a purchase as Fraud, and sent me a text message. When I called them to resolve the issue, I was on hold for over an hour. 

A few days later I attempted to access my credit card account on-line and I'm locked out, so I called and attempted to resolved the issue. I was told by someone who was obviously not a US Citizen, that they would send a link to my phone number and that I would need to take a picture and upload it to the link along with a copy of my drivers license. This seemed very supicious and I asked to speak with a US representative. The US Representative was telling me the same thing, so I asked for a supervisor because when I called in, the system recognized my phone number and matched it to my account. After talking to the supervisor, she offered to send me a passcode by mail that I could use to call in and verify myself. 

When I attempted to call back in to verify my account with the pascode I was mailed, Synchrony Bank refuses to accept the passcode they mailed me to verify myself and are demanding that I either upload a picture to them along with a copy of my drivers license or that I can mail them a copy of drivers license and a copy of my electric bill. As these are all items that can be used for identity theft I am refusing to do this. 

I believe that the fact that they will not accept the passcode that the mailed me via the US Mail should be adequate to prove I am who I say I am- and if they will not accept it, then that is Mail Fraud. 

I have tried to escalate the issue within Synchrony Bank, but the Account Manager I spoke with ( sorry I didn't get a name ) would not escalate to anyone. 

I refuse to follow their prescribed method for verifying my identity ( clicking on an unknown link and taking a video/photo of myself and uploading a copy of my drivers license ) or mailing them the same. 

I do not want this to affect my credit, however I can not verify any purchases made on the card as they refuse to mail me a statement or allow me access to the account on-line to verify the charges.

It becomes a self-fulfilling prophecy, i.e., scores reduced, limits reduced, scores reduced further, etc. WHY DON'T YOU GET IT?!? 

Further, CapitalOne 's explanation letter ( attached ) used a different credit bureau report and score which was more than a month outdated from the date of my request. CapitalOne aggressively markets their " XXXX '' product ( see history attached ) yet they use a different bureau and score for limit determination? This is deceptive, improper, and unethical- and should be illegal. As you can see, my score at the time of the request was significantly higher. Further, the XXXX score I see was XXXX at that same time. CapitalOne is improperly " cherry picking '' bureaus and/or scores to support whatever determination they want- in this case, denial of returning my limit to previous.

_source.complaint_what_happened:
I wrote this letter to various company offices. They have promised to reimburse me for over a month. I believe that this error occurs often everyday and they keep customers money. It is a systemic problem. Here is a copy of the letter sent and NOTHING has happened despite promises. As I said it is a very suspicion practice by this bank since errors of this type happen very often ALL representatives and managers tell me that it is protocol and standard instructions and it takes 60 days to return the money!! 
LETTER SEND TO BANK OFFICERS XX/XX/year> To VARIOUS BANK CORPORATE OFFICERS, PLEASE EXCUSE THE PROTRACTED MAIL BUT NECESSARY.. 
I am a XXXX XXXX year old retired college professor ( XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ) with visual impairments. My family and I have maintained a longstanding relationship with Bank of America spanning decades. For well over a decade, I have held a credit card ( ending in XXXX ) with your institution. The purpose of this correspondence is to address a recent cash advance transaction of {$24000.00}, which has resulted in an unfortunate misunderstanding. I have made similar sized transactions and have always paid them back without such a problem. Approximately {$12000.00} is remaining of the debt. 
After your staff and myself spent an hour on the phone trying to resolve my issue I was told that I must wait TWO billing cycles ( equivalent to XXXX DAYS ) to receive the {$2700.00} payment back to me due to an error of your employee!! 
I must express my concern regarding the absence of a clearly defined protocol or set of instructions by BoA to address this situation of communication error between a teller and a customer. Frankly, I find it quite suspicious that BoA does not have a very specific protocol or set of instructions to resolve this situation in a timely manner, unless it is part of their plan to detain payment of funds. 
On XX/XX/year>, I visited my local Bank of America XXXX XXXX located at XXXX XXXX XXXX in XXXX, Massachusetts to cash two checks, totaling {$2000.00} and {$1700.00} respectively, and to make a {$1000.00} payment toward the remaining balance of {$12000.00} on my credit card. I articulated my request in very clear XXXX by my initial statement which was, Hi, I would like to cash these two checks and make a {$1000.00} payment on my credit card. I said this very clearly in XXXX to the cashier, reiterating it more than four times during our interaction. I wish to emphasize that XXXX is my native language, and my communication was unambiguous. It is not the cashier 's native language. 
Regrettably, despite my explicit instructions, the cashier, whose primary language is not XXXX, applied the entire sum of both checks to the credit card balance, resulting in the absence of cash disbursement. When I realized the error, I promptly sought assistance from a manager, who acknowledged a potential " communication error. '' Although I acknowledge partial responsibility due to my inability to read the keypad agreement without my glasses, I firmly believe that my repeated verbal instructions should have sufficed to convey my intentions accurately.
